q: A 75-year-old man with recently diagnosed subclinical hypothyroidism (initial TSH 8.2) returns after eight weeks of levothyroxine 25 micrograms daily. He feels more energetic and again walks his dog daily, but his wife reports new evening confusion. TSH is 2.8, free T4 is 1.3 ng/dL, and temperature is 36.8 degrees C. His medications include levothyroxine, atorvastatin 40 mg, and diphenhydramine 50 mg nightly for sleep. Which statement about diphenhydramine supports reviewing its use in this patient?
o: Its short half-life makes residual sedation uncommon the next day.
Its adverse effects include delirium and decreased cognition in older patients.
Its sedating effect is maintained with repeated use because tolerance develops slowly.
Its adverse-effect profile supports using it as primary insomnia treatment.
explanation:
Diphenhydramine can impair cognition through anticholinergic effects. **Review it as a potential contributor to new confusion** even when thyroid indices have normalized.

**A. Short half-life** Its long half-life can cause next-day sedation.
**B. Delirium and decreased cognition** Both are recognized adverse effects in older adults.
**C. Slow tolerance** Tolerance to sedation can develop rapidly.
**D. Suitable primary insomnia therapy** Cognitive effects, retention and residual drowsiness argue against using it routinely for sleep.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 661.

q: An older woman is found in a cold home with a core temperature of 34.5 degrees Celsius. After the acute episode is treated, which assessment is appropriate to evaluate risk factors for recurrence?
o: Assess thyroid disease while omitting housing conditions
Assess medical, cognitive, social, and economic factors
Assess chronological age while omitting reversible factors
Assess room temperature while omitting protective responses
explanation:
Hypothermia can recur when exposure coincides with impaired thermoregulation or inability to seek warmth. **Assess medical, cognitive, social and economic contributors**, including whether she can heat her home.

**A. Thyroid assessment alone.** Hypothyroidism matters, but correcting it cannot solve an inadequately heated home.
**B. Multidomain assessment.** Review illness, medications, recognition of cold, access to heat and help obtaining it.
**C. Age alone.** Age identifies vulnerability without identifying what can be changed.
**D. Room temperature alone.** She may also be unable to sense cold, add clothing or call for help.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 582.
ref: Hazzard Ch 39 — SYSTEMS PHYSIOLOGY OF AGING AND SELECTED DISORDERS OF HOMEOSTASIS

q: An older adult with a history of prolonged corticosteroid treatment is being evaluated for possible adrenal insufficiency. Which assessment does Hazzard describe as the basis for a definitive diagnosis?
o: Measure basal serum cortisol to assess unstimulated adrenal hormone secretion.
Measure serum cortisol following corticotropin to assess stimulated adrenal secretion.
Measure TSH and free thyroxine to assess thyroid hormone secretion.
Measure fasting blood glucose to assess the current glycemic state.
explanation:
Cosyntropin is a synthetic ACTH analogue used to test whether the adrenal cortex can increase cortisol production when stimulated. **Measure serum cortisol after corticotropin to assess adrenal reserve.**

**A. Basal cortisol** — Morning cortisol can guide assessment of adrenal recovery. A borderline basal result alone does not measure stimulated reserve. Morning cortisol is usually the first test of recovery during a steroid taper when testing is needed.
**B. Stimulated cortisol** — A subnormal peak at thirty or sixty minutes supports insufficiency. Use the cutoff validated for the cortisol assay.
**C. Thyroid testing** — TSH and free thyroxine assess a different endocrine axis.
**D. Fasting glucose** — Hypoglycemia can accompany cortisol deficiency, but a glucose level cannot measure adrenal reserve.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 1531. Endocrine Society primary adrenal insufficiency guideline, recommendation 2.1. ESE/Endocrine Society glucocorticoid-induced adrenal insufficiency guideline (2024), recommendations 2.7–2.8.
ref: Hazzard Ch 97 — AGING OF THE ENDOCRINE SYSTEM AND NON-THYROID ENDOCRINE DISORDERS
chapterTitle: Aging of the Endocrine System and Non-Thyroid Endocrine Disorders

q: A 77-year-old woman with permanent primary hypothyroidism and ischemic heart disease is starting hormone replacement. Which approach to levothyroxine treatment is appropriate at her age?
o: Titrate levothyroxine cautiously toward a TSH near the upper normal limit
Titrate levothyroxine cautiously toward a suppressed TSH below the normal range
Replace levothyroxine with T3 to provide more physiologic hormone replacement
Stop levothyroxine after TSH normalizes to complete the cure of hypothyroidism
explanation:
Levothyroxine replaces the T4 a failing thyroid cannot supply. In an older adult with ischemic heart disease, **start cautiously and titrate toward the upper normal TSH range**.

**A. Cautious titration and upper-normal TSH** This allows adequate replacement while avoiding excess thyroid stimulation of the heart. Wait for a stable response before increasing again.
**B. Cautious titration to suppressed TSH** Deliberate suppression would create a risk of atrial fibrillation and bone loss during routine replacement.
**C. Replace T4 with T3** Tissues produce T3 from T4 as needed. Taking T3 can produce excessive levels and cardiac effects.
**D. Stop after normalization** A normal TSH shows the replacement dose is working. Permanent failure generally requires lifelong treatment.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 1552, Management of hypothyroidism.

q: An 86-year-old nursing-home resident with moderate Alzheimer dementia had three episodes of low measured body temperature (35.5-35.8°C) last winter despite adequate heating. Each episode improved with passive warming. His medications are donepezil 10 mg, risperidone 0.25 mg twice daily, gabapentin 300 mg three times daily, and docusate. Thyroid and metabolic testing is normal. While reviewing medications and other contributors, which principle should guide assessment for hypothermia?
o: Interpret limited cold exposure as insufficient evidence for ruling out hypothermia in older adults.
Use the absence of feeling cold as evidence against the diagnosis of hypothermia.
Use the absence of shivering as evidence against the need for temperature measurement.
Interpret adequate indoor heating as evidence that a low reading reflects thermometer error.
explanation:
Older adults may cool substantially without extreme environmental exposure or conspicuous shivering. **A heated setting cannot rule out hypothermia**. Verify core temperature with an appropriate thermometer. The previous readings above 35°C indicate low temperature without meeting the usual core definition.

**A. Limited cold exposure.** Impaired thermoregulation, illness or medications can produce cooling indoors.
**B. No complaint of feeling cold.** Dementia or impaired temperature perception can obscure this symptom.
**C. No shivering.** Shivering may be absent. A temperature measurement is more reliable than this sign.
**D. Indoor heating proves measurement error.** Verify the measurement and assess the patient instead of dismissing a low reading.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 582–583.
ref: Hazzard Ch 39 — SYSTEMS PHYSIOLOGY OF AGING AND SELECTED DISORDERS OF HOMEOSTASIS

q: An 84-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes, stage 3a chronic kidney disease (eGFR 45), and mild cognitive impairment is brought to the emergency department after her daughter finds her confused. Glucose is 42 mg/dL, sodium is 138, and creatinine is 1.8. Her medications include glipizide 10 mg twice daily, metformin 1000 mg twice daily, and lisinopril 20 mg daily. She lives alone and frequently skips meals. After the acute episode has been treated, which medication approach addresses the hypoglycemia concern described by Hazzard?
o: Replace glipizide with glyburide and review her meal schedule
Replace glipizide with a DPP-4 inhibitor; review metformin dosing
Continue glipizide and replace metformin with a DPP-4 inhibitor
Continue glipizide and metformin and review her meal schedule
explanation:
Glipizide drives insulin secretion even when a meal is skipped. A DPP-4 inhibitor instead prolongs glucose-dependent incretin signaling and has low hypoglycemia risk alone.

**Replace glipizide with a DPP-4 inhibitor if another agent is needed, and review metformin dosing for eGFR 45.** A glucose of 42 with confusion establishes that the present regimen is dangerous.

**A. Substitute glyburide.** Its longer half-life increases the risk of prolonged hypoglycemia.
**B. Replace glipizide and review metformin.** This removes the secretagogue and checks an independent renal dosing issue. Renal requirements differ among DPP-4 inhibitors.
**C. Replace metformin but retain glipizide.** The drug most likely to drive another low would still be present.
**D. Review meals alone.** Regular meals help, but continuing the culprit after severe hypoglycemia leaves substantial risk.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp1576–1577, 1579–1580.

q: A 79-year-old man with heart failure has leg edema, jugular venous distension, and mild pulmonary edema. Serum sodium is 124 mEq/L and has remained similar for four days; serum osmolality is low. He is fully alert, with no seizures or new neurologic symptoms. Which approach matches the hypervolemic hyponatremia described?
o: Give isotonic saline to correct volume depletion, with sodium monitoring
Increase water intake to promote sodium excretion, with sodium monitoring
Give a loop diuretic and restrict water intake, with sodium monitoring
Give hypertonic saline for a neurologic emergency, with sodium monitoring
explanation:
Heart failure can cause water retention out of proportion to sodium, producing low serum sodium despite excess extracellular fluid. **Use loop diuresis and water restriction with sodium monitoring** for this stable, congested patient.

**A. Isotonic saline.** It expands volume and targets depletion, whereas jugular distension and pulmonary edema indicate overload.
**B. More water.** Extra water can dilute serum sodium further and worsen congestion.
**C. Loop diuretic and water restriction.** Remove excess fluid while limiting further dilution and tracking the sodium response.
**D. Emergency hypertonic saline.** He is alert with stable sodium over several days and no severe neurologic symptoms.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 587.
ref: Hazzard Ch 39 — SYSTEMS PHYSIOLOGY OF AGING AND SELECTED DISORDERS OF HOMEOSTASIS

q: An 81-year-old woman with hyponatremia takes a thiazide and sertraline. Which approach to medication review follows the 2023 AGS Beers Criteria?
o: Consider the thiazide contribution and decrease sodium-monitoring frequency
Consider both medications and monitor sodium when treatment is changed
Consider the sertraline contribution and decrease sodium-monitoring frequency
Consider the combination protective and continue treatment without sodium monitoring
explanation:
Thiazides and SSRIs can each contribute to hyponatremia. In a patient already affected, both medicines belong in the review.

**Assess the thiazide and sertraline and follow sodium closely when treatment changes.** The medication list alone cannot determine their relative contributions.

**A. Consider only the thiazide and check less often.** This omits the SSRI and relaxes monitoring despite existing hyponatremia.
**B. Consider both and monitor.** Reviewing both exposures and repeating sodium can help guide treatment safely.
**C. Consider only sertraline and check less often.** This overlooks the diuretic and could miss worsening hyponatremia.
**D. Assume the combination is protective.** Both medicines can contribute to lower sodium, so continuing without surveillance leaves the hazard unassessed.

Reference · 2023 AGS Beers Criteria, p. 2068.

q: A 77-year-old man with hypernatremia and substantial volume depletion presents with hypotension that jeopardizes his cardiovascular status. Which sequence of fluid treatment is described in Hazzard?
o: Give free water initially, then change to isotonic saline
Give isotonic saline initially, then change to hypotonic fluid
Restrict fluid initially, then change to giving isotonic saline
Give free water initially, then maintain restriction of oral intake
explanation:
Hypernatremia denotes a water deficit relative to sodium, but severe hypotension first demands restoration of circulating volume. **Start isotonic saline, then replace the water deficit with more hypotonic fluid** once perfusion improves.

**A. Free water first.** It distributes beyond the circulation and is a poor initial resuscitation fluid in shock.
**B. Isotonic then hypotonic.** The first step restores perfusion. The second corrects hypertonicity with serial sodium measurements.
**C. Restrict then give saline.** Restriction delays treatment of threatened circulation.
**D. Free water then oral restriction.** This misses the initial resuscitation need and the subsequent need for ongoing water replacement.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 588.
ref: Hazzard Ch 39 — SYSTEMS PHYSIOLOGY OF AGING AND SELECTED DISORDERS OF HOMEOSTASIS

q: An 86-year-old woman develops hyponatremia with very poor food intake. Evaluation documents low daily solute excretion without evidence of excessive ADH secretion. Which mechanism explains the contribution of low solute availability?
o: Increased water excretion produces a rise in serum sodium.
Increased water excretion produces dilution of serum sodium.
Restricted water excretion produces a rise in serum sodium.
Restricted water excretion produces dilution of serum sodium.
explanation:
The maximum volume of water the kidneys can excrete depends partly on how much solute must be eliminated. With very low solute intake, **water excretion is limited and retained water dilutes serum sodium**, even without excess ADH.

**A. More water excretion, higher sodium.** Water loss could concentrate sodium, but low solute reduces excretory capacity.
**B. More water excretion, lower sodium.** Excreting free water opposes dilution.
**C. Restricted excretion, higher sodium.** Restricted clearance retains water and pushes sodium in the opposite direction.
**D. Restricted excretion, lower sodium.** Even a modest water intake can exceed the amount excretable with very little dietary solute.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 586.
ref: Hazzard Ch 39 — SYSTEMS PHYSIOLOGY OF AGING AND SELECTED DISORDERS OF HOMEOSTASIS

q: A 75-year-old man is hospitalized with hyponatremia after diarrhea. Assessment shows weight loss, orthostatic hypotension, and volume depletion without edema. There is no seizure or reduction in consciousness. Which approach targets the mechanism of this hyponatremia?
o: Restore volume with isotonic saline.
Reduce volume with an intravenous loop diuretic.
Reduce volume with strict fluid restriction.
Restore volume with a hypotonic glucose solution.
explanation:
Diarrheal losses can deplete extracellular volume and stimulate antidiuretic hormone, leading to dilutional hyponatremia. **Restore volume with isotonic saline**, then follow sodium as water excretion recovers.

**A. Isotonic saline.** It replaces salt and water lost in diarrhea and supports circulation.
**B. Loop diuretic.** More diuresis would worsen documented depletion.
**C. Strict fluid restriction.** Restriction cannot restore lost circulating volume.
**D. Hypotonic glucose solution.** It adds free water and can aggravate hyponatremia without providing adequate salt replacement.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 587.
ref: Hazzard Ch 39 — SYSTEMS PHYSIOLOGY OF AGING AND SELECTED DISORDERS OF HOMEOSTASIS
chapterTitle: Systems Physiology of Aging and Selected Disorders of Homeostasis

q: A woman treated for hypertension develops hyponatremia and hypokalemia. Which drug class is linked to this pattern in Hazzard’s table of antihypertensive medications for older adults?
o: Treatment with angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors
Treatment with thiazide-type diuretic medications
Treatment with calcium channel antagonists
Treatment with angiotensin receptor blockers
explanation:
Diuretic-associated electrolyte disturbance can present as weakness, confusion or a fall. **A thiazide-type diuretic can cause both hyponatremia and hypokalemia**, particularly in an older patient.

**A. ACE inhibitors** — Reduced aldosterone activity more often raises potassium. This is a poor match for concurrent sodium and potassium depletion.
**B. Thiazide-type diuretics** — Thiazides impair urinary dilution and promote renal potassium loss. Check sodium and potassium after starting or increasing the dose.
**C. Calcium-channel antagonists** — Peripheral edema is common with dihydropyridines. Constipation or slowed conduction can occur with certain agents, but the electrolyte pair is atypical.
**D. Angiotensin receptor blockers** — Like ACE inhibitors, ARBs can raise potassium, especially when renal function is impaired.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 1225–1226, Table 79-4.

q: A 78-year-old man with mild Alzheimer dementia and diabetes has become more confused over two days. He lives with his wife, who manages his medications. Serum sodium is 122 mEq/L. She recently gave him additional 'water tablets' for swollen ankles. Which medication-history focus is specifically supported by Hazzard's discussion of hyponatremia?
o: Clarify thiazide exposure as a cause of falsely low sodium without a water-balance disturbance
Clarify thiazide exposure as a cause of high sodium from impaired water retention
Clarify thiazide exposure as a recognized medication-related contributor to low sodium
Clarify thiazide exposure as evidence favoring gastrointestinal rather than medication-related sodium loss
explanation:
Thiazide diuretics are important causes of true hyponatremia in older adults. **Identify the exact water tablet, dose and timing of the additional doses** while assessing his confusion and sodium of 122.

**A. Falsely low sodium.** Thiazides can cause a real disturbance of renal sodium and water handling.
**B. High sodium.** The drug-related electrolyte pattern under consideration is low sodium.
**C. Thiazide-associated low sodium.** Recent extra doses make medication reconciliation particularly important. Assess other contributors as well.
**D. Gastrointestinal loss.** There is no reported gastrointestinal loss. The history points directly to possible excess diuretic exposure.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 586–587.
ref: Hazzard Ch 39 — SYSTEMS PHYSIOLOGY OF AGING AND SELECTED DISORDERS OF HOMEOSTASIS

q: An 85-year-old nursing home resident with advanced dementia and dysphagia receives thickened liquids. She is less responsive, with sodium 168 mEq/L, BUN 88, creatinine 2.1, and urine specific gravity 1.030. Staff report refusal of thickened water but acceptance of pudding and ice cream. Which mechanism fits the reported intake and a renal concentrating response?
o: Renal water loss accompanied by failure to concentrate the urine
Inadequate water intake accompanied by a concentrated urinary response
Renal water excretion accompanied by appropriately dilute urine in hyponatremia
Preserved water intake accompanied by continued loss of dilute urine
explanation:
Hypernatremia develops when water losses exceed intake. **Refusal of thickened drinks with concentrated urine favors inadequate intake and renal water conservation**. Her severe hypernatremia and reduced responsiveness require urgent assessment.

**A. Renal concentrating failure.** A concentrating defect usually causes inappropriately dilute urine and often polyuria.
**B. Poor intake with concentrated urine.** Dementia and dysphagia limit access to water, while the urine indicates a concentrating response.
**C. Dilute urine in hyponatremia.** Both the serum sodium direction and the urine pattern are reversed.
**D. Preserved intake with dilute losses.** Neither adequate drinking nor dilute urine is described.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 588.
ref: Hazzard Ch 39 — SYSTEMS PHYSIOLOGY OF AGING AND SELECTED DISORDERS OF HOMEOSTASIS

q: A 73-year-old woman taking warfarin starts using ginkgo biloba extract. Which interaction is described in Hazzard?
o: A lower bleeding risk when ginkgo is combined with warfarin
A lower drug-interaction risk when herbal medicines are added
A higher bleeding risk when ginkgo is combined with warfarin
A lower adverse-event risk when herbal use is left unreviewed
explanation:
Warfarin inhibits coagulation, and ginkgo constituents may inhibit platelet activation or aggregation. **Ginkgo taken with warfarin can add bleeding risk**, although the size and consistency of that interaction are not firmly established. Ask about the specific preparation, timing and bleeding symptoms.

**A. Lower bleeding risk.** A potential antiplatelet effect acts in the same hazardous direction as anticoagulation for bleeding, rather than protecting against it.
**B. Herbal medicines lower interaction risk.** Supplement ingredients and doses vary and can add interactions even when prescribed drug doses have not changed.
**C. Higher bleeding risk.** Bleeding has been reported with combined use, including an association in observational data. This supports reviewing the combination without predicting an exact risk for this woman.
**D. Leave supplements unreviewed.** An incomplete medication list can conceal contributors to bruising or hemorrhage; a normal INR would not measure a potential platelet effect.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 302. Ginkgo and Warfarin Interaction in a Large Veterans Administration Population, PMCID PMC4765589.
ref: Hazzard Ch 22 — MEDICATION PRESCRIBING AND DE-PRESCRIBING

q: An older adult taking spironolactone starts trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole. Which electrolyte risk does Hazzard emphasize for this combination?
o: Development of significant hyperkalemia during treatment
Development of hypokalemia from the combined medications
A sustained potassium decrease requiring preventive supplementation
Potassium loss that offsets the effect of spironolactone
explanation:
Trimethoprim and spironolactone both impair distal potassium secretion. Together they can cause **marked hyperkalemia**, particularly when renal reserve is reduced.

**A. Hyperkalemia.** The two potassium-retaining effects add together, making monitoring important.
**B. Hypokalemia.** Neither drug produces the potassium wasting that would explain a low concentration here.
**C. Preventive potassium replacement.** Supplementation adds to potassium retention and can worsen the interaction.
**D. Offsetting potassium loss.** Trimethoprim reinforces, rather than counteracts, spironolactone's potassium-sparing effect.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 1271.
ref: Hazzard Ch 82 — AGING OF THE KIDNEY

q: A 76-year-old woman develops postoperative hyponatremia while receiving medication. Evaluation supports SIADH. Which urine finding supports impaired free-water excretion?
o: Dilute urine indicating increased excretion of free water
Dilute urine indicating appropriate suppression of ADH activity
Concentrated urine despite the low serum sodium concentration
Low-solute urine indicating preserved ability to dilute urine
explanation:
SIADH causes continued water reabsorption despite hypotonicity. **The urine remains inappropriately concentrated while serum sodium is low.**

**A. Dilute urine indicating increased excretion of free water.** A normally dilute urine indicates the kidney can excrete excess water.
**B. Dilute urine indicating appropriate suppression of ADH activity.** Appropriate suppression of ADH is the response that fails in SIADH.
**C. Concentrated urine despite the low serum sodium concentration.** Continued ADH effect prevents maximal dilution, often leaving urine osmolality above 100 mOsm/kg.
**D. Low-solute urine indicating preserved ability to dilute urine.** Low solute intake can itself limit water excretion. Preserved maximal dilution is a different mechanism.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 587.
ref: Hazzard Ch 39 — SYSTEMS PHYSIOLOGY OF AGING AND SELECTED DISORDERS OF HOMEOSTASIS

q: An 83-year-old man with mild cognitive impairment and diabetes presents with fatigue and poor oral intake. His daughter manages his metformin and glimepiride. Sodium is 156, glucose 680, and calculated osmolality 348. She has also given him her furosemide for swelling. Which renal mechanism can link uncontrolled hyperglycemia to the water deficit, without establishing its contribution relative to poor intake or diuretic exposure?
o: Enhanced urinary concentration that increases renal water conservation
Osmotic diuresis that increases renal water loss
Extrarenal water loss caused by reduced access to drinking fluids
Suppressed urinary output that accompanies increased water conservation
explanation:
Severe hyperglycemia can produce urinary glucose that draws water into urine. **Osmotic diuresis increases renal water loss** and can contribute to hypernatremia alongside poor intake or a diuretic.

**A. Enhanced concentration.** Renal conservation limits water loss. It does not explain glucose-driven diuresis.
**B. Osmotic diuresis.** Glucose in tubular fluid retains water there, increasing urine volume and the water deficit.
**C. Poor access to fluids.** This can contribute independently through low intake, but it is not a renal loss mechanism.
**D. Suppressed urine output.** This is a conserving response, the opposite of glucose-induced polyuria.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 588.
ref: Hazzard Ch 39 — SYSTEMS PHYSIOLOGY OF AGING AND SELECTED DISORDERS OF HOMEOSTASIS

q: A nursing-home resident has inadequate relief of constipation with docusate. What is Hazzard's rationale for considering another treatment?
o: Its frequent use in nursing homes demonstrates established laxative efficacy
Its limited laxative effect favors considering a more effective alternative
It has the highest level of evidence among the agents discussed
It has demonstrated quality-of-life benefits in constipation treatment trials
explanation:
Frequent prescribing does not measure whether patients actually pass stool more comfortably. Docusate has little effect on colonic motility, and comparative evidence favors more active treatments.
**Replace ineffective docusate with an agent better matched to the patient’s symptoms.**

**A. Frequency of use proves efficacy.** Common prescribing can coexist with undertreated constipation and impaction.
**B. Limited laxative effect.** Persistent symptoms warrant assessment for retention and a more effective regimen.
**C. Highest evidence level.** PEG has stronger evidence for adult constipation.
**D. Established quality-of-life benefit.** A quality-of-life improvement with docusate has not been demonstrated in these patients.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 1372, 1376.

q: A woman with hypernatremia is hemodynamically stable and requires correction of a water deficit. Which principle should guide treatment?
o: Replace water while adjusting treatment and monitoring serum sodium
Prescribe a fixed water volume based on the initial calculation
Restrict water as the main means of lowering serum sodium
Use isotonic saline as the main means of replacing free water
explanation:
A stable patient with hypernatremia needs replacement of missing water. **Estimate the deficit, replace water and adjust to serial sodium values and ongoing losses**.

**A. Monitored water replacement.** The response shows whether the estimated deficit and loss rate were accurate.
**B. Fixed calculated volume.** A calculation cannot anticipate changing intake, renal losses or ongoing illness.
**C. Restrict water.** This increases the water deficit and can worsen hypertonicity.
**D. Isotonic saline as principal replacement.** Use it first when circulation is threatened. A stable water deficit requires water or a suitable hypotonic fluid.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 588.
ref: Hazzard Ch 39 — SYSTEMS PHYSIOLOGY OF AGING AND SELECTED DISORDERS OF HOMEOSTASIS

q: An 84-year-old man with diabetes, hypertension and mild cognitive impairment (MMSE 22) presents after 3 days of productive cough, fever and delirium. He has fallen twice that day and missed medications. His usual drugs are metformin 1000 mg twice daily, lisinopril 20 mg daily and atorvastatin 40 mg daily. Temperature is 38.8°C, BP 95/60 mmHg, pulse 110/min, respiratory rate 28/min and oxygen saturation 88% on room air. Chest radiography shows right lower-lobe consolidation; WBC is 16.2, creatinine 2.1 mg/dL (baseline 1.2) and glucose 340 mg/dL. Oxygenation and hemodynamic support are being addressed. Which infection-directed strategy accords with Hazzard while microbiology results are pending?
o: Start oseltamivir and reassess before adding antibacterial treatment
Start ceftriaxone plus azithromycin while awaiting microbiology results
Correct hyperglycemia and volume depletion before starting antimicrobial treatment
Obtain viral PCR and use the result to decide on initial antibacterials
explanation:
Community-acquired pneumonia with hypoxemia and hypotension warrants prompt empiric antibacterial therapy. This man's lobar consolidation and acute delirium justify **starting ceftriaxone plus azithromycin while microbiology is pending**.

**A. Oseltamivir first.** Oseltamivir treats influenza. If influenza is suspected, it can be added promptly while bacterial pneumonia is also treated.
**B. Ceftriaxone plus azithromycin.** Ceftriaxone covers pneumococcus and other common bacterial causes. Azithromycin adds activity against atypical pathogens such as Legionella.
**C. Correct glucose and volume first.** Resuscitation and glucose management can proceed alongside antibiotics. Neither addresses the pulmonary infection.
**D. Wait for viral PCR.** A respiratory virus can coexist with bacterial pneumonia. PCR can help refine treatment without delaying the first antibiotic dose.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 1688–1689.
ref: Hazzard Ch 105 — BACTERIAL PNEUMONIA AND TUBERCULOSIS

q: A 79-year-old woman has acute pulmonary embolism, is hemodynamically stable, and has no active bleeding. Creatinine clearance is 22 mL/min. Inpatient treatment is selected, with a need to stop and reverse anticoagulation rapidly if necessary. Which option best fits Hazzard's recommendations?
o: Start oral warfarin and follow INR until the therapeutic range is reached
Start oral dabigatran and monitor renal function and bleeding during treatment
Start an intravenous UFH infusion and adjust treatment using coagulation tests
Start oral rivaroxaban and monitor renal function and bleeding during treatment
explanation:
For an inpatient with PE, severe renal impairment and a need for rapid reversibility, **use titratable intravenous unfractionated heparin**. Its short half-life and protamine reversibility can be advantageous.

**A. Warfarin alone.** Its delayed onset makes it unsuitable as the sole initial anticoagulant for acute PE.
**B. Oral dabigatran.** It relies heavily on renal elimination and requires preceding parenteral treatment for acute VTE.
**C. IV UFH.** Adjust using the local aPTT or anti-Xa protocol and monitor for bleeding and thrombocytopenia.
**D. Rivaroxaban.** It does not offer the same immediate infusion control, particularly when drug clearance is impaired.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, Ch 96, p. 1520.

q: An 88-year-old man with falls takes trazodone for sleep and asks to add a sedative. After evaluating his sleep problem, which approach reduces exposure to centrally acting medications?
o: Consider replacing trazodone with zolpidem for sleep
Consider behavioral insomnia treatment and medication review
Consider replacing trazodone with lorazepam for sleep
Consider adding clonazepam to trazodone for sleep
explanation:
A patient already taking trazodone for sleep may be exposed to more sedation if a second drug is added. **Review the existing medication and consider behavioral insomnia treatment.**

**A. Replace trazodone with zolpidem** — Zolpidem remains a centrally acting hypnotic associated with falls and confusion.
**B. Behavioral treatment and medication review** — Review whether the current drug helps, identify drivers of poor sleep and address them without adding another sedative.
**C. Replace it with lorazepam** — Lorazepam adds benzodiazepine-related impairment of balance and psychomotor function.
**D. Add clonazepam** — Combining two centrally acting drugs increases sedative burden, particularly concerning in someone who has already fallen.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 639 and 659.

q: An older woman with influenza develops bacterial pneumonia as a complication. Which pair of organisms does Hazzard specifically identify as infections to which influenza predisposes patients?
o: E. coli and E. faecalis.
P. aeruginosa and K. pneumoniae.
S. pneumoniae and S. aureus.
M. pneumoniae and C. pneumoniae.
explanation:
Influenza can be complicated by secondary bacterial pneumonia. New fever or respiratory deterioration after initial improvement should raise concern for **Streptococcus pneumoniae or Staphylococcus aureus**.

**A. E. coli and E. faecalis.** E. coli commonly causes urinary infection, and enterococci are unusual causes of pneumonia.
**B. P. aeruginosa and K. pneumoniae.** Both can cause gram-negative pneumonia. Prior respiratory isolation of Pseudomonas would point toward it more specifically than a history of influenza.
**C. S. pneumoniae and S. aureus.** Pneumococcus is a frequent cause of secondary pneumonia, and rapid deterioration after influenza raises particular concern for staphylococcal pneumonia.
**D. M. pneumoniae and C. pneumoniae.** These atypical bacteria usually cause primary community-acquired pneumonia. A preceding influenza illness points more strongly toward pneumococcus or S. aureus.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 1734. ATS/IDSA, Community-Acquired Pneumonia Guideline, 2019.
ref: Hazzard Ch 108 — INFLUENZA, COVID-19, AND OTHER RESPIRATORY VIRUSES
chapterTitle: Influenza, COVID-19, and Other Respiratory Viruses

q: An 81-year-old man is hospitalized with a complicated urinary tract infection, fever, flank pain, and hypotension. Why should nitrofurantoin and fosfomycin not be selected for this infection?
o: Inadequate penetration into renal tissue for treating complicated urinary infection.
Insufficient antibacterial activity within the bladder during acute simple cystitis.
Limited activity against multidrug-resistant isolates, particularly in the case of fosfomycin.
Excessive penetration into renal tissue, making these drugs unsuitable for older patients.
explanation:
Fever, flank pain and hypotension suggest kidney infection with systemic illness rather than isolated cystitis. **Inadequate renal tissue exposure** makes nitrofurantoin and oral fosfomycin unsuitable here.

**A. Insufficient renal penetration.** Treatment must reach renal parenchyma and provide systemic coverage when the patient is unstable.
**B. Insufficient bladder activity.** These drugs can be useful for selected bladder infections. The infected site is different.
**C. Limited activity against resistant isolates.** Even a susceptible isolate would not overcome inadequate tissue exposure.
**D. Excessive renal penetration.** This reverses the pharmacologic problem.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 1708, 1711.

q: A 77-year-old woman is hospitalized with community-acquired pneumonia and is receiving ceftriaxone. Legionella infection cannot be excluded, and she has no contraindication to a macrolide. Which antibiotic plan agrees with Hazzard while investigations continue?
o: Add azithromycin as a single 500 mg dose alongside ceftriaxone.
Use amoxicillin-clavulanate instead of combining a beta-lactam antibiotic with azithromycin.
Withhold ceftriaxone temporarily while waiting for identification of the pathogen.
Add azithromycin 500 mg daily while continuing treatment with ceftriaxone.
explanation:
Legionella is an intracellular cause of pneumonia that beta-lactams do not cover reliably. In this hospitalized woman, **continue ceftriaxone and add azithromycin 500 mg once daily** while investigations continue.

**A. One dose of azithromycin.** A single 500 mg dose starts the regimen. Continued empiric treatment for possible Legionella requires repeat daily dosing.
**B. Substitute amoxicillin-clavulanate.** Clavulanate inhibits some beta-lactamases. It does not give amoxicillin reliable activity against Legionella.
**C. Pause ceftriaxone.** Holding it would interrupt treatment for common bacterial causes such as pneumococcus before the pathogen is known.
**D. Continue ceftriaxone and add daily azithromycin.** The macrolide reaches intracellular Legionella while the beta-lactam maintains coverage for pneumococcus and other common bacterial pathogens.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 1689, Table 105-11.
ref: Hazzard Ch 105 — BACTERIAL PNEUMONIA AND TUBERCULOSIS

q: אישה בת 85 מאושפזת עם herpes zoster הפוגע ב-dermatome של V1 ימני. יש לה דמנציה מסוג אלצהיימר מתונה והיא גרה עם בתה. Creatinine הוא 1.3 mg/dL (CrCl של 28 mL/min לפי Cockcroft-Gault), משקל 48 ק"ג. הפריחה הופיעה לפני יומיים. תרופות נוכחיות: memantine 10mg BID, escitalopram 10mg ביום. היא אלרגית לסולפה (פריחה). מהו הטיפול האנטי-ויראלי המתאים?
o: Acyclovir 800mg PO 5 פעמים ביום למשך 7 ימים
Valacyclovir 1000mg PO TID למשך 7 ימים
Famciclovir 500mg PO TID למשך 7 ימים
Acyclovir 400mg PO TID למשך 7 ימים
explanation:
שלבקת חוגרת באזור הענף העיני של העצב הטריגמינלי עלולה לפגוע בקרנית ובראייה. מתחילים טיפול אנטי־נגיפי סיסטמי בהקדם ובודקים אם נדרשת התערבות עינית.
**בפינוי הקריאטינין הנתון, 28 מ״ל לדקה, אציקלוביר 800 מ״ג דרך הפה חמש פעמים ביום למשך שבעה ימים הוא משטר מתאים מבין האפשרויות.** יש לעקוב אחר תפקוד הכליות והיכולת לשתות.

**A. אציקלוביר 800 מ״ג חמש פעמים ביום.** בפינוי מעל 25 מ״ל לדקה טבלת המינון מאפשרת את המרווח הרגיל לטיפול בזוסטר. הפריחה החלה לפני יומיים.
**B. ולאציקלוביר 1,000 מ״ג שלוש פעמים ביום.** בפינוי של 10–29 מ״ל לדקה המרווח לטיפול בזוסטר הוא פעם ביממה. שלוש מנות ביום עלולות להצטבר.
**C. פמציקלוביר 500 מ״ג שלוש פעמים ביום.** בפינוי של 20–39 מ״ל לדקה נדרשת מנה של 500 מ״ג פעם ביממה.
**D. אציקלוביר 400 מ״ג שלוש פעמים ביום.** המנה קטנה מהמנה לטיפול בשלבקת. אם תפקוד הכליה יורד עוד, מאריכים את המרווח בין מנות ה־800 מ״ג בהתאם לפינוי.

אסמכתא · Hazzard 8e, עמ׳ 1727–1728, טבלה 107-1. עלוני DailyMed לאציקלוביר, טבלה 3, ולוולאציקלוביר ולפמציקלוביר, טבלה 1.
retiredReason: Hazzard 8e (marked), p.1727 Table 107-1: famciclovir 500 mg q8h, valacyclovir 1 g q8h and acyclovir 800 mg five times daily for 7 days are all listed regimens, and the acyclovir regimen is footnoted 'Adjust acyclovir dosing for renal function' with no adjusted dose given. With CrCl 28 the keyed unadjusted acyclovir conflicts with that footnote, two other options are book regimens, and the explanation's 400 mg TID is not in the book, so there is no single source-supported answer.

q: A 78-year-old man with COPD and impaired kidney function has symptomatic influenza that began one day ago. Which antiviral approach is consistent with Hazzard?
o: Give oseltamivir at a treatment dose adjusted for his kidney function
Give oseltamivir at a prophylactic dose during his symptomatic influenza illness
Give inhaled zanamivir because of its advantage in obstructive lung disease
Give amantadine to treat the influenza A strains circulating in the community
explanation:
Oseltamivir treats influenza A and B. This 78-year-old has COPD, is at increased risk of complications and became ill yesterday. **Start oral oseltamivir promptly at a treatment dose matched to his kidney function.**

**A. Renally adjusted treatment.** The kidneys clear oseltamivir's active metabolite. Use creatinine clearance to select the appropriate treatment regimen.
**B. Prophylactic oseltamivir.** Prophylaxis aims to prevent influenza in someone who is still asymptomatic. Its dosing can undertreat active influenza.
**C. Inhaled zanamivir.** It can trigger bronchospasm in someone with COPD and worsen respiratory distress.
**D. Amantadine.** Resistance is widespread among circulating influenza A viruses, and amantadine has no activity against influenza B.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 1736. CDC, Influenza Antiviral Medications.
ref: Hazzard Ch 108 — INFLUENZA, COVID-19, AND OTHER RESPIRATORY VIRUSES
chapterTitle: Influenza, COVID-19, and Other Respiratory Viruses

q: An 82-year-old woman in a nursing facility for rehabilitation after a hip fracture develops sudden confusion and agitation. She repeatedly pulls at her Foley catheter. She has hypertension, osteoporosis, and mild cognitive impairment. Her medications include amlodipine 5 mg, weekly alendronate, vitamin D, oxycodone 5 mg as needed every 6 hours, and docusate. Vital signs are normal. Urinalysis shows 50–100 white blood cells, positive nitrites, and numerous bacteria. Creatinine is 1.1 and her weight is 58 kg. Which interpretation of the findings is supported by Hazzard?
o: Attribute the acute confusion to urinary infection on the basis of the positive urinalysis.
Exclude an infectious cause of acute confusion because her current vital signs are normal.
Postpone evaluation for other causes of acute confusion while waiting for urine culture results.
Evaluate for infection and alternative causes of acute confusion before attributing it to urinary infection.
explanation:
Delirium needs a clinical search for precipitants. Catheterized patients commonly have bacteria and white cells in urine. **Assess for infection and alternative causes before attributing the acute change to UTI.**

**A. Assume UTI from urinalysis.** Catheter-associated bacteriuria and pyuria can occur without symptomatic infection.
**B. Exclude infection from normal vital signs.** An older adult may lack fever. Vitals are only one part of the assessment.
**C. Wait for culture before evaluating anything else.** This can delay identification of pain, retention, medications or another acute illness.
**D. Evaluate both possibilities.** Examine for urinary or systemic signs and assess other delirium precipitants in parallel.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 1703, 1707.

q: A patient with advanced illness has refractory breathlessness despite optimal treatment of the underlying cause. Which statement is appropriate when considering an opioid trial for relief?
o: Favor morphine in renal insufficiency because its accumulating metabolites are protective
Replace cause-directed treatment with an opioid trial as the initial approach
Weigh relief of breathlessness against deterioration in mental functioning
Expect improved cognitive function to accompany the relief of breathlessness
explanation:
Opioids used for refractory dyspnea supplement treatment of the underlying cause. **Weigh improvement in breathlessness against possible loss of alertness or cognition**.

**A. Morphine metabolites protect in CKD.** Reduced renal clearance can increase neurotoxicity.
**B. Replace cause-directed care.** Treat reversible contributors before labeling the symptom refractory.
**C. Weigh relief and alertness.** Patient preferences help determine whether a monitored trial is worthwhile.
**D. Expect cognitive improvement.** Dyspnea may improve while cognition worsens.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 1074.
ref: Hazzard Ch 69 — MANAGEMENT OF COMMON NONPAIN SYMPTOMS

q: An older woman requests an antibiotic despite the absence of a clinical indication. Which statement about treatment risks in older adults agrees with Hazzard?
o: Reduced renal function favors routine dosing because sensitivity to adverse effects is lower
Renal function and polypharmacy require attention to dose adjustment and drug interactions
Polypharmacy makes selection easier because concurrent medications reduce interaction concerns
Increasing age favors routine dosing because antibiotic adverse-effect sensitivity tends to diminish
explanation:
An antibiotic without a clinical indication exposes the patient to adverse effects without an expected benefit. **Check kidney function and the medication list** whenever an antibiotic is actually needed.

**A. Use routine doses despite reduced kidney function** — Reduced clearance may prolong exposure to renally eliminated drugs and can require a change in maintenance dosing.
**B. Assess renal dosing and interactions** — A clearance estimate and medication review help select a drug, dose and interval that achieve treatment goals while limiting harm.
**C. More medicines simplify selection** — More concurrent drugs create more opportunities for interactions, toxicity and dosing errors.
**D. Adverse effects diminish with age** — Older adults can be more susceptible to adverse drug effects, especially with reduced clearance or limited physiologic reserve.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 1670.
ref: Hazzard Ch 104 — INFECTION AND APPROPRIATE ANTIMICROBIAL SELECTION

q: An older man with COPD has a mild exacerbation suitable for outpatient treatment. What initial adjustment to bronchodilator therapy does Hazzard recommend?
o: Increase short-acting inhaled bronchodilator treatment during the exacerbation
Stop inhaled bronchodilator treatment during the mild exacerbation
Reduce usual maintenance treatment during the mild exacerbation
Delay bronchodilator escalation until initial antibiotic treatment fails
explanation:
An acute exacerbation increases airflow obstruction. A rapidly acting inhaled bronchodilator can ease that obstruction promptly and may suffice in a mild episode.
**Increase short-acting inhaled bronchodilator treatment while continuing usual maintenance treatment.**

**A. Increase short-acting treatment.** Use an inhaled short-acting β₂ agonist, with or without a short-acting anticholinergic, and reassess the response.
**B. Stop bronchodilators.** Withdrawing them removes the principal treatment for acute bronchoconstriction.
**C. Reduce the maintenance regimen.** Usual maintenance therapy generally continues during a mild exacerbation.
**D. Wait for antibiotics to fail.** Bronchodilation addresses the airflow problem immediately. Antibiotics address a separate indication.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 1260.
ref: Hazzard Ch 81 — CHRONIC OBSTRUCTIVE PULMONARY DISEASE

q: An 86-year-old woman with truncal herpes zoster presents 48 hours after rash onset. She is immunocompetent, creatinine clearance is 65 mL/min, and there is no ocular involvement. Which virus-directed treatment is appropriate to reduce acute pain and the duration of chronic pain according to Hazzard?
o: Oral gabapentin adjusted according to tolerability
Oral valacyclovir for a full seven-day course
Topical acyclovir applied over the affected skin
Oral prednisone followed by a gradual dose taper
explanation:
Systemic antiviral treatment started early in shingles reduces acute pain and can shorten persistent pain. She presents at 48 hours with localized truncal disease and a creatinine clearance of 65 mL/min. **Give valacyclovir 1 g orally three times daily for seven days.**

**A. Oral gabapentin.** It can relieve neuropathic pain when analgesia is inadequate. It has no antiviral activity.
**B. Oral valacyclovir.** Her rash began within the 72-hour treatment window studied, and her renal function permits the usual zoster regimen.
**C. Topical acyclovir.** Applying antiviral cream to the vesicles provides no meaningful benefit for shingles.
**D. Oral prednisone.** Occasionally used alongside an antiviral for severe acute pain, prednisone alone does not treat zoster or prevent postherpetic neuralgia.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 1727–1728. Valacyclovir prescribing information, Table 1.
ref: Hazzard Ch 107 — OTHER VIRUSES: HUMAN IMMUNODEFICIENCY VIRUS INFECTION AND HERPES ZOSTER
chapterTitle: Other Viruses: Human Immunodeficiency Virus Infection and Herpes Zoster

q: אדם עם דמנציה מתקדמת מתקשה באכילה. איזה תהליך לבחירת דרך ההזנה תואם את המלצות הוועדה הארצית?
o: בחירת דרך ההזנה לפי משך הירידה באכילה
בחירת דרך ההזנה לפי רמת האלבומין בדם
בחירת דרך ההזנה לפי אבחנת הדמנציה הקיימת
בחירת דרך ההזנה לפי הערכה אישית ורב־מקצועית
explanation:
בתת־תזונה ובקושי באכילה אצל אדם עם קיהיון אין מדד יחיד שבוחר את הדרך. בוחנים בליעה, בטיחות, מצב רפואי ויכולת לספק סיוע. **בחירת דרך ההזנה לפי הערכה אישית ורב־מקצועית**.

**א. בחירת דרך ההזנה לפי משך הירידה באכילה.** משך ההפרעה הוא נתון אחד ואינו קובע את המסלול.
**ב. בחירת דרך ההזנה לפי רמת האלבומין בדם.** אלבומין מושפע גם ממחלה ודלקת.
**ג. בחירת דרך ההזנה לפי אבחנת הדמנציה הקיימת.** אבחנת דמנציה אינה מודדת בליעה או צורך בצינור.
**ד. בחירת דרך ההזנה לפי הערכה אישית ורב־מקצועית.** הערכה אישית של הצוות מחברת בין הממצאים לתוכנית ולהעדפות.

אסמכתא · המלצות הוועדה הארצית על הזנה בדמנציה, עמ׳ 5, סעיפים ד עד ו.

q: An 83-year-old woman develops diarrhea and colitis after antibiotic treatment during hospitalization. Clostridium difficile infection is diagnosed. Which mechanism explains the association with antibiotic exposure?
o: An allergic response to the antibiotic directly damages the colonic mucosa
An osmotic action of the antibiotic draws fluid into the intestinal lumen
An antibiotic-related neural injury disrupts intestinal propulsive activity
Alteration of normal colonic flora permits disease caused by the organism
explanation:
Intestinal microbes normally help protect against C. difficile infection. **Antibiotic-related disruption of normal flora** explains why diarrhea and colitis can develop after treatment.

**A. Drug allergy.** A hypersensitivity reaction does not explain the diagnosed infectious colitis.
**B. Osmotic drug effect.** Some medicines cause osmotic diarrhea, but that mechanism does not explain C. difficile colitis.
**C. Neural injury.** Impaired motility is a different cause of bowel dysfunction.
**D. Disrupted colonic flora.** Loss of normal microbial protection increases susceptibility to symptomatic infection.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 1304.
ref: Hazzard Ch 84 — AGING OF THE GASTROINTESTINAL SYSTEM AND SELECTED LOWER GI DISORDERS

q: בן 78, הסובל מדמנציה מתקדמת מאושפז במחלקה לסיעוד מורכב עקב פצע לחץ דרגה 4 בטרוכנטר. לאחרונה נצפתה החמרה בהפרשה מהפצע, הופיע אודם מקומי ונמדד חום סיסטמי 38.5. מה הגישה הטיפולית לזיהום במקרה המתואר?
o: מתן טיפול אנטיביוטי בהתאם לבדיקת מטוש (SWAB) ממוגלה שיוצאת מהפצע
מתן טיפול אנטיביוטי ראשוני המכסה זיהום ב- PSEUDOMONAS AUROGINOSA
מתן טיפול אנטיביוטי ב- CEFAMEZIN היעיל בטיפול בחיידקי עור כמו STREPTOCOCUS ו- STAPHILOCOCUS
מתן טיפול אנטיביוטי אמפירי רחב טווח
explanation:
A chronic pressure wound can carry bacteria for months. New drainage, spreading redness and fever raise concern that infection has invaded tissue and may have reached the bloodstream.

**Start broad empiric systemic antibiotics.** Cover gram-positive cocci, aerobic gram-negative rods and anaerobes while obtaining appropriate cultures, then narrow treatment to the organisms causing infection.

**A. Surface pus swab.** Drainage contains organisms living on the wound surface. Sampling viable deep tissue after cleansing gives more reliable information for targeted therapy.
**B. Pseudomonas coverage alone.** Pseudomonas is one possible pathogen. A deep infected pressure injury can contain several species, including anaerobes and staphylococci.
**C. Cefazolin alone.** Cefazolin covers many susceptible skin organisms. It leaves gaps in the coverage needed when a deep wound is accompanied by fever.
**D. Broad empiric antibiotics.** The combination of systemic illness and local deterioration warrants treatment before culture results return.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 695, 697.

q: בת 78, אקדמאית בהשכלתה, עצמאית בכל התפקודים אובחנה לאחרונה כסובלת ממחלת אלצהיימר בדרגת חומרה קלה. היא מדווחת על הפרעה בעיקר בזיכרון לטווח הקצר אשר מפריעה לה במשחק ברידג' ובניהול כספים. באבחון הקוגניטיבי שעברה במסגרת הבירור נעשתה בדיקת MOCA המצורפת: המטופלת ובעלה מבקשים לדעת האם מומלץ לבצע תרגול קוגניטיבי ומאיזה סוג. מהי ההמלצה הנכונה?
o: מומלץ לבצע תרגול קוגניטיבי בתחומים שהיו לקויים באבחון כמו הזיכרון והריכוז
מומלץ לבצע תרגול קוגניטיבי בתחומים שנמצאו שמורים באבחון, לדוגמא בתחום השפתי ובתחום התפיסה החזותית מרחבית
מומלץ להימנע מתרגול קוגניטיבי מאחר ואינו יעל והוא עשוי להוביל לתסכול ולדיכאון
מומלץ להמשיך ולהשתתף בפעילות לגירוי קוגניטיבי לצורך עניין והנאה בלבד
explanation:
Cognitive activity works best when it is achievable and meaningful. **Build on the individual tasks she performed successfully and use compensatory strategies for valued tasks affected by memory loss.** Her MoCA shows successful animal naming, cube copying and clock drawing; it does not certify that every language or visual-executive ability is intact.

**A. Train impaired memory and concentration.** Goal-directed rehabilitation can help with specific tasks such as tracking bids or checking payments. Repeated unsuccessful drills are a different approach and can cause frustration.
**B. Use preserved abilities.** Naming and selected drawing tasks offer practical starting points. She missed the alternating trail and verbal fluency items, so tailor difficulty within each domain.
**C. Avoid all cognitive activity.** Supported participation can sustain engagement and daily skills even when recall is poor.
**D. Enjoyment only.** Pleasure matters, and realistic goals can also include confidence, task completion and participation.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 915. Attached Hebrew MoCA, version 8.1, named-item and visuospatial/executive rows.

q: בן 92 הסובל מדמנציה מתקדמת, מאושפז מזה חודש במחלקת קורונה. בקבלתו המוגלובין 12.8. במהלך האשפוז הופיעו פצעי לחץ דרגה 4 בשני הטרוכנטרים. כעת סובל גם מ- MRSA SEPSIS. בבדיקות המעבדה: מדד ויחידות המטופל ערכים תקינים WBC 10e3qµL 12,800 4.0-11.0 HgB gr/dl 9.5 17 - 13.2 MCV fL 80 80-96 PLT 10e3qµL 496,000 140-450 NEU % 82 40-75 LYM % 16 20-40 IRON µg/dL 32 40-150 TRANSFERRIN mg/dL 152 220-400 FERRITIN ng/dL 188 14-163 VIT B12 pg/mL >1000 175-961 FOLIC ACID ng/mL 3.6 2.6-17 BUN mg/dL 24 5-25 CREATININE mg/dL 0.5 0.7-1.3 ALBUMIN g/L 26 35-50 CRP mg/L 158 0.03-5.0 מה האבחנה והטיפול המומלץ לאנמיה?
o: מדובר קרוב לודאי ב- MYELOSYSPLASTIC SYNDROME ומומלץ לתת טיפול ב- ERTHROPOIETIN
מדובר באנמיה מחסר ברזל ומומלץ טיפול בברזל תוך ורידי
לא ניתן לאבחן את סוג האנמיה ללא בדיקת מח עצם ולכן לא ניתן להמליץ על טיפול
מדובר באנמיה של מחלה כרונית. רק שיפור במצבו הזיהומי ישפר את האנמיה
explanation:
Inflammation restricts the release of stored iron and suppresses erythropoiesis. Low circulating iron can therefore coexist with low transferrin and preserved or increased ferritin.

**The falling hemoglobin during MRSA sepsis and deep pressure injuries fits anemia of inflammation. Treat the infection and reassess as it resolves.**

**A. Myelodysplasia and erythropoietin.** The new anemia tracks a severe infection, with high CRP and reactive changes in white cells and platelets. There is little here to point first to a clonal marrow disorder.
**B. Absolute iron deficiency and intravenous iron.** The low transferrin and increased ferritin favor inflammatory iron restriction. Low serum iron alone is insufficient grounds for intravenous replacement.
**C. Marrow examination before any decision.** The timing, inflammatory markers and iron profile already support a working diagnosis. Persistent anemia after recovery warrants reevaluation.
**D. Anemia of chronic disease and infection control.** In this setting the inflammatory trigger is active infection. Treating it addresses the mechanism restricting iron use and red-cell production.

Reference · Harrison, pp. 629–630 (2020 exam bibliography). Corresponding material in Harrison 21e, pp. 752–753, Figure 97-4 and Table 97-6.

אשפוז לצורך בדיקת מח עצם בחשד ל- ACUTE LEUKEMIA
שחרור למעקב מרפאה המטולוגית בחשד ל- CHRONIC LYMPHOCYTIC LEUKEMIA
שחרור עם המלצה לטיפול ב- G-CSF עקב נויטרופניה אסימפטומטית ומעקב מרפאה המטולוגית בהקדם
explanation:
An incidental absolute lymphocytosis with small mature lymphocytes and a smudge cell suggests CLL. **Arrange outpatient hematology assessment and peripheral-blood flow cytometry** for this stable man with preserved hemoglobin and platelets.

**A. Inpatient antibiotics** — The fall and leukocytosis alone provide no clinical focus of infection. The differential shows lymphocyte predominance.
**B. Urgent marrow examination for acute leukemia** — The film shows mature lymphoid cells, and the other blood counts are preserved. Blood immunophenotyping is usually sufficient for suspected CLL.
**C. Outpatient hematology follow-up** — Confirm a characteristic clonal B-cell population and assess persistence, symptoms, nodes and spleen. Asymptomatic early disease is generally observed.
**D. G-CSF for neutropenia** — Eleven percent of 31,200 white cells is about 3,400 neutrophils per microliter. The low percentage masks a preserved absolute count.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 1490–1491.

q: בת 81, הולכת עם מקל מאז ניתוח החלפת ברך. ברקע יתר ל"ד. נוטלת LERCANIDIPINE (VASODIP). אושפזה במחלקה קרדיולוגית בעקבות NSTEMI שטופל באמצעות צנתור שכלל הנחת תומכן. אקו לב הדגים תפקוד סיסטולי מעט ירוד של חדר שמאל (LVEF 45%). כעת מיועדת לשחרור לביתה. סימנים חיוניים שנלקחו יום לפני השחרור - ל"ד 125/82, דופק 59 ובבוקר השחרור – ל"ד 116/80, דופק 58. בשחרור הומלץ על טיפול ב- ASPIRIN, CLOPIDOGREL (PLAVIX) ו- ATORVASTATIN (LIPITOR). איזו מבין רשימות תרופות הבאות מתאימה להשלמת התרופות המומלצות בשחרור:
o: LERCANIDIPINE (VASODIP), BISOPROLOL (CARDILOC)
LERCANIDIPINE (VASODIP), RAMIPRIL (TRITACE)
RAMIPRIL (TRITACE)
BISOPROLOL (CARDILOC)
explanation:
After an infarction, discharge therapy should reduce recurrent risk without provoking bradycardia or hypotension. ACE inhibition is useful after MI with impaired ventricular function and also treats hypertension.
**Add ramipril alone from the listed regimens. Her EF is mildly reduced, her resting pulse is already 58–59, and her pressure is controlled. Recheck blood pressure, potassium and creatinine after initiation.**

**A. Lercanidipine and bisoprolol.** These add blood-pressure lowering and further rate slowing while omitting an ACE inhibitor.
**B. Lercanidipine and ramipril.** Ramipril addresses ventricular dysfunction, whereas adding a second blood-pressure agent at 116/80 adds hypotension risk without a stated need.
**C. Ramipril.** It provides the missing renin–angiotensin blockade without further slowing her resting heart rate.
**D. Bisoprolol.** Beta blockade can benefit selected post-MI patients, but her repeated resting rate below 60 makes it a poor first addition among these options.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, ch. 74, pp. 1140–1141, 1143, 1147 (parallel teaching for the 2020 question).

q: בן 75, עצמאי ב- BADL. ברקע - סכרת ואי ספיקת לב, מטופל ב- DAPAGLIFUZIN (FORXIGA), LINAGLIPTIN (TRAJENTA), METFORMIN, ENALAPRIL ו- DISOTHIAZIDE. התקבל לאשפוז אלקטיבי לניתוח TKR שבוצע ללא אירועים חריגים. ביממה השנייה לאחר הניתוח חלה ירידה במצב ההכרה, החולה נמצא ישנוני ומבולבל. ל"ד 90/60 דופק 100 סדיר, סטורציה תקינה, חום תקין. במעבדה: בדיקה ויחידות ערך לחולה ערכי נורמה BUN mg/dL 80 25 - 5 CREATININE mg/dL 1.7 0.6-1.1 NA mmol/L 145 135-146 K mmol/L 4.5 3.5-5.3 Cl mmol/L 88 95-110 PH 7.0 7.35-7.45 PCO2 mmHg 35 35-46 HCO3 mmol/L 14 21-26 בבדיקת שתן: לויקוציטים +, תאים אדומים -, ניטריט -, קטונים +++ תופעת לוואי של איזו מהתרופות הבאות עשויה להיות הגורם למצבו של החולה?
o: METFORMIN
DAPAGLIFLOZIN (FORXIGA)
LINAGLIPTINE (TRAJENTA)
DISOTHIAZIDE
explanation:
Marked ketonuria with postoperative acidosis points to ketoacid production. SGLT2 inhibition can promote ketoacidosis during illness or fasting even without striking hyperglycemia.

**Dapagliflozin is the drug linked to this presentation.** Hypotension, low bicarbonate and substantial ketonuria support the diagnosis even though a glucose result was not supplied.

**A. Metformin.** Hypoperfusion and renal dysfunction raise concern for lactic acidosis. That alone would not explain marked ketonuria.
**B. Dapagliflozin.** Surgery, fasting and fluid loss can precipitate ketosis. Stop dapagliflozin now. Check blood glucose, beta-hydroxybutyrate and electrolytes urgently, and treat ketoacidosis even if glucose is near normal. For a future elective procedure, withhold dapagliflozin at least three days beforehand.
**C. Linagliptin.** This DPP-4 inhibitor increases glucose-dependent incretin action. Ketotic acidosis is not its characteristic adverse effect.
**D. Hydrochlorothiazide.** A thiazide can contribute to volume depletion or electrolyte disturbances, but does not ordinarily cause ketoacidosis.

Reference · Hazzard 7e, p1659. Hazzard 8e, pp. 1578, 1580, 1585. ADA Standards of Care 2026, §16, perioperative care. Hyperglycemic Crises in Adults With Diabetes, 2024 consensus report, Table 4.

q: הממשלה מעוניינת לבדוק כדאיות חיסון לקורונה בקרב אנשים בני פחות מ- 60 שגרים עם קשישים באותו בית. על פי הפרסום "בני 65+ בישראל" מה אחוז הקשישים שגר עם ילדיו בבית?
o: 0.5% מהקשישים גרים במשק בית של זוג עם ילדים, 0.5% גרים במשק בית של הורה יחיד עם ילדים
2% מהקשישים גרים במשק בית של זוג עם ילדים, 1% גרים במשק בית של הורה יחיד עם ילדים
12% מהקשישים גרים במשק בית של זוג עם ילדים, 5% גרים במשק בית של הורה יחיד עם ילדים
24% מהקשישים גרים במשק בית של זוג עם ילדים, 12% גרים במשק בית של הורה יחיד עם ילדים
explanation:
**כ־12% גרו במשק בית של זוג עם ילדים וכ־5% במשק של הורה יחיד עם ילדים.** לוח 1.34 מתייחס לבני 65 ומעלה בישראל בשנת 2022.

**א. 0.5% ו־0.5%.** שני השיעורים נמוכים בסדר גודל מן הנתונים.
**ב. 2% ו־1%.** שני האומדנים נמוכים מהערכים הנמדדים.
**ג. 12% ו־5%.** אלו העיגולים של 11.6% ו־4.9%, בהתאמה.
**ד. 24% ו־12%.** השיעורים גבוהים מן הנתונים לשתי קטגוריות המגורים.

אסמכתא · מכון ברוקדייל, בני 65+ בישראל, שנתון 2024, עמ׳ 118, לוח 1.34.

q: בת 82, מאושפזת מזה כשבועיים בטיפול נמרץ באבחנה של דלקת ריאות, כשהיא מונשמת ומטופלת באנטיביוטיקה וסטרואידים IV.תחת הטיפול נצפה שיפור קליני במצבה. בשל הופעת פרפור עליות במהלך האשפוז נלקחה בדיקה לתפקודי בלוטת התריס. להלן התוצאות. מדד ויחידות ערך לחולה ערכי נורמה TSH mU/L <0.01 0.4-4.7 T4 ng/dl <0.1 0.7-1.8 T3 pg/ml <0.01 1.71-3.71 מה ההסבר לשינוי בבדיקות וההמלצה הטיפולית?
o: מדובר בהיפותירואידזם מרכזי, יש להשלים בדיקות מעבדה לשלול מחלה היפופיזרית נוספת, ולהתחיל בהקדם טיפול ב- IV LEVOTHROXIN
מדובר ב- Non thyroidal illness syndrome ויש להתחיל טיפול ב- IV LEVOTHYROXINE
היות ובמצב זה תיתכן גם פגיעה באדרנל המשך טיפול בסטרואידים יתרום לעליה ב- TSH
אין השלכה קלינית לתוצאות בשלב זה, יש להמליץ על בדיקה חוזרת לתפקודי תריס בעוד כחודשיים
explanation:
Critical illness can lower T3, T4 and eventually TSH, and IV steroids may suppress TSH further. In this improving patient, **defer thyroid treatment and repeat testing after recovery**, as proposed at about two months.

**A. Treat central hypothyroidism** Low TSH and low T4 can mimic pituitary failure. Severe pneumonia and steroid exposure explain the pattern without other pituitary clues.
**B. Treat nonthyroidal illness with IV T4** The diagnosis fits but thyroid replacement has shown no benefit in this syndrome.
**C. Use steroids to raise TSH** High-dose glucocorticoids can lower TSH. Continuing them for pneumonia does not correct this thyroid-test pattern.
**D. Recheck after recovery** These results can mark severe illness but do not themselves call for thyroid replacement. Reassessment when stable can reveal any persistent disorder.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 1548, Nonthyroidal illness syndrome.

q: בת 78, פנתה למרפאה עקב חולשה וירידה במשקל של 5 ק"ג בשנה האחרונה. בן זוגה מדווח על ירידה מסויימת בזיכרון. לחץ הדם 128/62 עם ירידה ל- 102/45 בעמידה. בבדיקות המעבדה: בדיקה ויחידות ערך לחולה ערכי נורמה WBC 10e3qµL 6700 4.0-11.0 HgB gr/dl 10.8 17 - 13.2 PLT 10e3qµL 496,000 140-450 CREATININE mg/dL 0.5 0.7-1.3 BUN mg/dL 24 5-25 Na mmol/L 124 135-146 K mmol/L 5.4 3.5-5.3 מה סביר שיימצא בבדיקות המעבדה האנדוקריניות שלה?
o: רמת CRTISOL בשתן מעל מהנורמה
רמת TSH מתחת לנורמה
תגובה מופחתת למתן ACTH
תגובה מופחתת ל- LOW DOSE DEXAMETHASONE SUPRESSION TEST
explanation:
Cortisol deficiency causes weakness and weight loss. Concomitant aldosterone loss promotes sodium loss, postural hypotension and hyperkalemia. **Her sodium of 124, potassium of 5.4 and marked orthostatic fall suggest a blunted cortisol response to ACTH.**

**A. High urinary cortisol** — Excess cortisol would point toward hypercortisolism and does not fit this electrolyte pattern.
**B. Low TSH** — Thyroid testing alone would not explain the combination of salt loss, hyperkalemia and orthostasis.
**C. Reduced response to ACTH** — A failing adrenal cortex cannot mount a normal cortisol increase after stimulation.
**D. Abnormal dexamethasone suppression** — Failure to suppress after dexamethasone is used to investigate cortisol excess.

Reference · Hazzard 7e, p. 1610. Related Hazzard 8e teaching, p. 1531.

q: בן 82, מתגורר בביתו עם מטפל זר. ברקע - דמנציה מתקדמת, מרותק לכיסא גלגלים, נזקק לעזרה בכל צרכי ה- ADL. בנוסף, סוכרת, אי-ספיקת לב ופרפור פרוזדורים. לאחרונה קיבל טיפול אנטיביוטי ממושך עקב זיהום בדרכי השתן. התקבל למחלקה למלר"ד עקב ירידה במצבו הכללי, אירועי שלשול מימי מרובים עד 5 ליום וחום. בקבלתו למלר"ד לחץ דם 82/45, דופק 105, סטורציה 91% באוויר חדר, חום 37.8. בבדיקת צואה- CLOSTRIDIUM DIFFICILE TOXIN חיובי. בבדיקות המעבדה: מדד ויחידות החולה ערכים תקינים WBC 10e3qµL 18,700 4.0-11.0 HgB gr/dl 13.2 17 - 13.2 MCV Fl 78 80-96 PLT 10e3qµL 300,000 140-450 Na mmol/L 148 135-146 K mmol/L 3.2 3.5-5.3 CREATININE mg/dL 2 0.7-1.3 מה הטיפול האנטיביוטי המומלץ?
o: METRONIDAZOLE (FLAGYL) פומי
VANCOMYCIN פומי
METRONIDAZOLE (FLAGYL) פומי בשילוב עם LOPERAMIDE (IMODIUM) אחרי כל שלשול
VANCOMYCIN פומי ו- METRONIDAZOLE (FLAGYL) תוך ורידי
explanation:
Toxin-positive diarrhea with a blood pressure of 82/45 mmHg is fulminant C. difficile infection. **Give enteral vancomycin with intravenous metronidazole**, resuscitate promptly and assess for ileus, megacolon and the need for surgical input.

**A. Oral metronidazole** — This provides inadequate treatment for fulminant colitis with shock.
**B. Oral vancomycin alone** — Vancomycin reaches the colonic lumen, but fulminant disease calls for the intravenous adjunct, particularly when transit is impaired.
**C. Oral metronidazole and loperamide** — Suppressing motility in fulminant colitis can mask deterioration. This regimen also omits enteral vancomycin.
**D. Oral vancomycin and intravenous metronidazole** — High-dose enteral vancomycin treats the colonic infection. Intravenous metronidazole supplements treatment, and rectal vancomycin may be added if ileus limits delivery.

בת 74, חמישה ימים לאחר שחרורה מבית חולים על רקע החמרה באי ספיקת לב, הגיעה למעקב במרפאה. מתלוננת על קוצר בנשימה במאמץ. ברקע ידוע על מחלת לב איסכמית, יתר לחץ דם, אי ספיקת לב, פרפור פרוזדורים, יתר שומנים בדם, אי ספיקה כלייתית כרונית. תרופות:  
 VALSARTAN 160 mg X1  
 METOPROLOL 25 mg X1  
 FUROSEMIDE 40 mg X1  
 DIGOXIN 0.125 mg X1  
 APIXABAN 5 mg X2  
 SPIRONOLACTONE 12.5 mg X1

 בבדיקתה – ל"ד 126/76 בשכיבה, 128/78 בעמידה, דופק 77 לדקה, מספר נשימות 16 לדקה. אין ממצאים בהאזנה לריאות, אין סימנים של עודף נוזלים, משקל יציב. במעבדה: מדד ויחידות החולה ערכים תקינים Na mmol/L 136 135-146 K mmol/L 4.4 3.5-5.3 CREATININE mg/dL 1.6 0.7-1.3 BUN mg/dL 30 5-25 Digoxin ng/mL 1.4 0.8-2.0 מה היא הפעולה הטובה ביותר לביצוע בשלב זה ?
o: להפסיק טיפול ב- SPIRONOLACTONE
להעלות מינון FUSID לפעמיים ביום
להקטין מינון של VALSARTAN
להפסיק זמנית DIGOXIN ולחדש במינון מופחת
explanation:
Digoxin is cleared mainly by the kidneys. In this euvolemic woman with CKD and a controlled ventricular rate, **temporarily hold digoxin and restart at a lower dose if it remains indicated**. Her concentration of 1.4 ng/mL exceeds the usual low HF target.

**A. Stop spironolactone** Potassium is 4.4 and no new contraindication is specified. Review renal function and the need for potassium supplementation, but the high digoxin exposure is the clearer finding.
**B. Increase furosemide** Clear lungs, stable weight and no clinical congestion argue against intensifying diuresis solely for exertional dyspnea.
**C. Reduce valsartan** Blood pressure is preserved without orthostasis, and there is no stated potassium rise or acute renal deterioration to prompt this change.
**D. Hold and reduce digoxin** Verify sampling time, renal function, electrolytes and ongoing rate control. A laboratory upper limit of 2.0 ng/mL is not the therapeutic target for HF.

q: בן 72, ברקע severe aortic stenosis פונה למיון עם שלשול ממושך מזה 5 ימים מלווה בחולשה קיצונית ומיעוט במתן שתן. סימנים חיוניים- סטורציה 97%, ל"ד 80/40, דופק 120. בבדיקות מעבדה (בטבלה בהמשך) נמצאה אי ספיקה כלייתית חדה. הוחל טיפול בעירוי נוזלים. ביום למחרת- עדיין ממעט במתן שתן. מתלונן על קוצר נשימה. סימנים חיוניים- סטורציה 88%, ל"ד 130/80, דופק 98. בהאזנה לריאות ובצילום חזה- ממצאים מתאימים לגודש ריאתי. בדיקות המעבדה: מדד ויחידות החולה ערכים תקינים יום 1 יום 2 Na mmol/L 142 130 135-146 K mmol/L 6.8 6.2 3.5-5.3 CREATININE mg/dL 7.5 7.6 0.7-1.3 BUN mg/dL 77 58 5-25 Ph 7.21 7.28 7.34-7.45 PO2 mmHg 78 66 70-100 PCO2 mmHg 25 35 35-46 HCO3 mmol/L 15 18 21-26 אילו מבין הבאים הינו סיבה לדיאליזה דחופה בחולה זה?
o: עודף נוזלים
היפרקלמיה
קריאטנין מוגבר שלא יורד
חמצת מטבולית
explanation:
Urgent dialysis is considered when a life-threatening consequence of AKI cannot be controlled medically. After fluids, the patient is still oliguric and has new pulmonary edema and falling oxygen saturation. **Symptomatic fluid overload** is the immediate indication in this vignette.

**A. Fluid overload** — New dyspnea, pulmonary congestion and an oxygen saturation of 88% show that retained fluid is compromising gas exchange. Reassess oxygenation and the need for urgent fluid removal.
**B. Hyperkalemia** — Potassium of 6.2 mmol/L remains dangerous and needs prompt assessment and treatment. It has fallen from 6.8, and the vignette gives no ECG findings or failed potassium-lowering treatment to distinguish refractory hyperkalemia.
**C. Persistently elevated creatinine** — Creatinine measures loss of filtration. Its absolute value alone does not determine whether dialysis is urgent.
**D. Metabolic acidosis** — Acidosis can require dialysis when severe and refractory. The pH and bicarbonate have improved while the respiratory consequences of fluid overload have worsened.

Reference · Hazzard 7e, p. 1306, Table 88-2. Clinical comparison in Hazzard 8e, p. 1283.

q: בת 70 פנתה לברור עקב. כאב גב בהדמיה נמצא שבר בחוליה T8 ו. נגעים ליטיים מרובים במרפאה המטולוגית אובחנה כסובלת מ- IgG kappa MULTIPLE MYELOMA והוחל טיפול ב- DEXAMETASONE ו- BROTEZOMIDE (VELCADE). בבדיקות המעבדה: מדד ויחידות החולה ערכים תקינים Na mmol/L 138 135-146 K mmol/L 4.8 3.5-5.3 CREATININE mg/dL 1.2 0.7-1.3 BUN mg/dL 42 5-25 Ca mg/dL 9.1 8.5-10.5 Albumin g/L 36 35-50 WBC 10e3/µL 5.8 4.0-11.0 HgB g/dL 11.2 11.7-15.5 אשה Plt 10e3/µL 187 150-450 מה מבין התרופות הבאות היא המתאימה ביותר לחולה זו למניעת סיבוכים גרמיים?
o: denosumab ( prolia)
pamidronate (aredia)
Calcium supplement with vitamin D
Calcitonin
explanation:
Myeloma-associated osteolysis predisposes to additional fractures even when serum calcium is normal. **Intravenous pamidronate reduces skeletal events in active myeloma with lytic lesions.**

**A. Denosumab (Prolia)** — Denosumab also has a myeloma indication as the oncology formulation Xgeva, given at a different dose and interval. Prolia is the osteoporosis regimen named here.
**B. Pamidronate** — This intravenous bisphosphonate inhibits bone resorption and is appropriate for preventing further skeletal complications. Assess renal function before administration.
**C. Calcium and vitamin D** — Supplementation may support bone health when appropriate, but cannot replace a bone-modifying agent for myeloma-related lytic disease.
**D. Calcitonin** — Its short-term calcium-lowering role does not provide durable prevention of myeloma fractures. The patient's calcium is normal.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 1505; ASCO bone-modifying agents guideline, doi:10.1200/JCO.2017.76.6402; FDA Xgeva and Prolia prescribing information, sections 1–2.

q: בן 82 ללא מחלות רקע ידועות וללא טיפול תרופתי קבוע. פיתח פרפור פרוזדורים לאחרונה. הותחל טיפול תרופתי בנוגדי קרישה ובהמשך ב- AMIDARONE (PROCOR). בבדיקות מעבדה לאחר שבועיים: מדד ויחידות החולה ערכים תקינים TSH mu/L 7.8 0.4-4.7 FT4 ng/dL 2.3 0.7-1.8 TT3 ng/dL 55 60-180 כיצד יש להתערב בעקבות הפתולוגיה בבדיקות המעבדה?
o: מדובר בת ירו. טוקסיקוזיס יש להוסיף לטיפול תכשיר חוסם ביטא
מדובר בתופעת לואי שכיחה. במצב המתואר מומלץ מעקב בלבד
תמונה של תירואידיטיס. מומלץ לתת טיפול ב- Methimazole
מדובר בתופעת לואי נדירה ומסכנת חיים, יש להפסיק טיפול ב Amiodarone ולתת טיפול ב Elthroxin
explanation:
Early in amiodarone therapy, TSH may rise transiently while free T4 rises and T3 falls. **Monitor this expected pattern without adding thyroid treatment** in this otherwise stable patient.

**A. Add a beta blocker for thyrotoxicosis** Elevated TSH with a low T3 is unlike the suppressed TSH expected in overt thyrotoxicosis. The laboratory pattern alone does not call for additional rate control.
**B. Monitor** Amiodarone inhibits conversion of T4 to T3. The early TSH rise can settle without stopping an effective antiarrhythmic.
**C. Give methimazole for thyroiditis** Methimazole blocks new hormone synthesis. Destructive thyroiditis releases stored hormone and usually presents with low TSH.
**D. Stop amiodarone and give levothyroxine** A transient TSH increase together with high free T4 does not show overt primary hypothyroidism.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 1547–1548, Table 98-1 and amiodarone.

q: בן 84, עצמאי ושמור קוגניטיבית, ברקע סכרת, יתר לחץ דם. מתלונן על חולשה והרגשה כללית לא טובה מזה כחודשיים. מדווח על כאבים בכתפיים, יותר בשעות הבוקר. בבדיקות מעבדה - HB 10.1 עם MCV 65, ללא לויקוציטוזיס, כימיה בגדר הנורמה, רמת CRP -65. ראומטואיד פקטור חיובי, ANA שלילי. ב- EMG סימנים אופייניים של inflammatory myopathy. הועלה חשד ל- לPolymyalgia Rheumatica (PMR). איזה ממצא תורם לאבחון של PMR בחולה זה?
o: rheumatoid factor חיובי
ANA שלילי
ב- EMG סימנים אופייניים של inflammatory myopathy
אנמיה מיקרוציטית
explanation:
Polymyalgia rheumatica (PMR) is recognized by the pattern of girdle pain, morning stiffness and inflammation. **A negative antinuclear antibody (ANA) is compatible with PMR and is the best fit among these findings.** It is common enough in people without PMR that it has little diagnostic weight alone.

**A. Positive rheumatoid factor** — This finding raises the possibility of elderly-onset rheumatoid arthritis. Assess the joint pattern and consider anti-CCP antibodies.
**B. Negative ANA** — ANA is usually negative in PMR. The shoulder symptoms and elevated CRP provide stronger support in this patient.
**C. Inflammatory myopathy on EMG** — Such changes have rarely been described in PMR, but should prompt a search for inflammatory muscle disease, especially with objective weakness or elevated CK.
**D. Microcytic anemia** — Inflammation in PMR typically produces normocytic anemia. An MCV of 65 warrants a separate evaluation, including for iron deficiency.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 1601–1602, Table 100-3.

q: בן 83 אמור לעבור בעוד חודש ניתוח אלקטיבי של תיקון הרניה מפשעתית מימין. ברקע: מחלת לב איסכמית, אי ספיקת כליות כרונית, יתר לחץ דם וטרום סוכרת. באק"ג שגרתי נמצא RBBB. בבדיקות המעבדה לפני הניתוח- מדד ויחידות החולה ערכים תקינים Na mmol/L 142 135-146 K mmol/L 5.1 3.5-5.3 CREATININE mg/dL 2.2 0.7-1.3 BUN mg/dL 46 5-25 Glucose mg/dL 117 72-100 מה משפיע על הסיבוכים הקרדיאליים הצפויים לאחר הניתוח?
o: נוכחות טרום סוכרת
Mild Mitral regurgitation
קריאטינין >2
פתולוגיה בבדיקת אק"ג
explanation:
The Revised Cardiac Risk Index uses six preoperative features to estimate major cardiac complications after noncardiac surgery. **A creatinine of 2.2 mg/dL meets its renal criterion of greater than 2.0 mg/dL.**

**A. Prediabetes** The diabetes criterion is preoperative insulin treatment. A fasting glucose of 117 mg/dL does not fulfill it.
**B. Mild mitral regurgitation** Mild regurgitation is not one of the six risk-index variables. Symptomatic or severe valvular disease warrants separate assessment.
**C. Creatinine above 2 mg/dL** This patient has both renal impairment above the threshold and a history of ischemic heart disease, another index variable.
**D. Abnormal ECG** An isolated right bundle-branch block does not earn a point. Specific cardiac history and the other index variables determine the score.

Reference · IMA December 2021 Q36, Hazzard 7e, pp. 456–458. Lee et al., Circulation 1999, pp. 1043–1049, doi:10.1161/01.CIR.100.10.1043.

q: בן 88, סובל מפצע לחץ בטרוכנטר ימין. ראה תמונה 2. הוא מטופל בביתו ע"י משפחתו המעוניינים בטיפול האופטימלי עבור ומוכנים לקנות כל תכשיר. מה התכשיר המומלץ לניקוי הפצע לפני החלפת חבישה?
o: מי חמצן 3%
תמיסת NaCl 0.9%
מים מינרלים סטריליים
Polydin 10%
explanation:
Cleansing at dressing changes removes loose debris while protecting viable tissue. The photograph shows a partly red wound bed, and the history gives no clinical signs requiring treatment of invasive infection.

**Gently irrigate with 0.9% sodium chloride.** Isotonic saline is suitable for routine cleansing of viable tissue. Reassess separately if necrosis or infection develops.

**A. Hydrogen peroxide 3%.** Peroxide can injure the fibroblasts involved in repair and should be avoided on open pressure wounds.
**B. Sodium chloride 0.9%.** Gentle irrigation with this physiologic solution removes surface material without exposing the healing bed to an antiseptic.
**C. Sterile mineral water.** Water of suitable quality can also be used for routine wound cleansing. Sterile mineral water offers no specific advantage over the isotonic fluid listed here.
**D. Povidone-iodine 10%.** An antiseptic may have a role in a wound with substantial debris or infection. Routine application to clean, healing tissue can impair fibroblast activity.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 692–693, 697. WHS pressure ulcer guidelines, 2023 update, guideline 4.5.

q: בת 82 ברקע דמנציה עם הפרעות התנהגות קשות. דיירת מחלקה לתשושי נפש. מטופלת בין השאר ב- VENLAFAXINE (EFFEXOR), CLOZAPINE (LEPONEX), ALPRAZPLAM (XANAX) ו- ZOLPIDEM (ZODORM). הגיעה לחדר מיון עקב חום. בבדיקות מעבדה: מדד ויחידות החולה ערכים תקינים WBC 10e3/µL 2600 4.0-11.0 NEU % 29.5 40.0-75.0 NEU No. 10e3/µL 0.8 1.4-6.0 HgB g/dL 13.3 11.7-15.5 אשה Plt 10e3/µL 235 150-450 איזה מבין התרופות הבאות הינו הגורם להפרעה בספירת הדם בסבירות הגבוהה ביותר?
o: VENLAFAXINE (EFFEXOR)
CLOZAPINE (LEPONEX)
ALPRAZPLAM (XANAX)
ZOLPIDEM (ZODORM)
explanation:
Fever with an absolute neutrophil count of 800/µL warrants urgent infection assessment. **Clozapine is the most likely drug cause. Promptly interrupt or review it under the applicable ANC protocol**, repeat the count and arrange urgent infection management and hematology input. Normal hemoglobin and platelets do not make this safe for routine follow-up.

**A. Venlafaxine.** Hyponatremia is a better-recognized adverse effect. It is much less strongly associated with this neutropenic pattern.
**B. Clozapine.** It can cause severe neutropenia. In the standard general-population protocol, ANC between 500 and 999/µL calls for interruption and hematology review. Special baseline-neutropenia protocols can differ. Assess for sepsis and give prompt empiric antibiotics when indicated.
**C. Alprazolam.** Sedation and falls are important harms, but do not explain the isolated low ANC.
**D. Zolpidem.** Delirium and falls are characteristic geriatric risks, rather than marked neutropenia.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 928, 946–947. FDA Clozaril prescribing information, neutropenia dosage-modification tables and fever precautions.
