chapterTitle: Harrison 22e ch. 305 – Disorders of the Pleura
keySource: IMA 2024-Sep Basic official answer key after appeals, Q103
explanation:
Pleural-fluid protein and LDH ratios of 0.7 and 0.65 satisfy exudative criteria. Very low pleural glucose suggests a strongly inflammatory pleural process. **Rheumatoid pleuritis** best fits the listed diagnoses.

**A. Heart failure.** Heart failure usually causes a transudate. Diuresis can alter ratios, but very low glucose would still need another explanation.
**B. Nephrotic syndrome.** Nephrotic syndrome usually causes transudative fluid through low oncotic pressure.
**C. Pulmonary embolism.** Pulmonary embolism can cause an exudate, but severely reduced pleural glucose is less characteristic.
**D. Rheumatoid arthritis.** Rheumatoid effusions can be exudative with strikingly low glucose. Infection and malignancy also warrant consideration in practice.

Reference · Harrison 22e, pp. 2267–2268, 2270.

q:
בת 77 התחילה טיפול כימותרפי עקב Acute Myelocytic Leukemia.
איזו הפרעה מטבולית יכולה להופיע לאחר התחלת הטיפול?
o: היפרגליקמיה
היפרפוספטמיה
היפרקלצמיה
היפרתנרמיה
keySource: IMA 2024-Sep Basic official answer key after appeals, Q104
explanation:
Tumor lysis releases intracellular solutes after effective chemotherapy. **Hyperphosphatemia** is a characteristic finding, alongside hyperkalemia and hyperuricemia. Calcium can fall as it binds phosphate.

**A. Hyperglycemia.** Elevated glucose is not a defining consequence of rapid tumor-cell lysis.
**B. Hyperphosphatemia.** Intracellular phosphate enters the bloodstream as large numbers of cells break down.
**C. Hypercalcemia.** The characteristic calcium disturbance is in the opposite direction.
**D. Hypernatremia.** Sodium elevation is not part of the typical tumor-lysis pattern.

Reference · Harrison 22e, p. 593.

בת 78, מאושפזת במחלקה פנימית, מתלוננת על כאבים באזור פי הטבעת ושלשולים מימיים מזה יומיים. סימנים חיוניים תקינים. בבדיקת הבטן – בטן רכה, לא רגישה. בבדיקות המעבדה ללא עליית מדדי דלקת, עליה קלה בתפקודי כליה. בדיקות צואה שליליות לפרזיטים וקלוסטרידיום.

קולונוסקופיה
בדיקת CT בטן
תרבית צואה חוזרת
keySource: IMA 2024-Sep Basic official answer key after appeals, Q105
explanation:
Watery leakage can pass around retained hard stool and mimic infectious diarrhea. In this older patient with rectal symptoms, **perform a digital rectal examination** to identify a potentially reversible impaction.

**A. Rectal examination.** A bedside examination can detect a hard mass and directly change management.
**B. Colonoscopy.** Endoscopy can be needed for persistent or concerning symptoms, but it is not the first way to identify an accessible stool plug.
**C. Abdominal CT.** CT is useful when complications or proximal disease are suspected. It need not precede a focused bedside assessment.
**D. Repeat stool culture.** Another stool culture would not address overflow from impaction.

Reference · Harrison 22e, pp. 305–306.

q:
בת 74 אושפזה לבירור עלית חום עד 38.5 מזה שבוע. בתרבית דם אחת התקבלה צמיחה של Srep. VIRIDANS. בהאזנה ללב – אוושה חדשה שלא היתה בעבר. אקו לב (TTE) לא הדגים פתולוגיה משמעותית.
איזה מידע נוסף יאפשר לאבחן על פי DUKE CRITERIA שמדובר באנדוקרדיטיס?
o: ממצא פתולוגי אופייני ב- TEE
הנתונים הקיימים מספיקים לאבחנה של אנדוקרדיטיס
פתולוגיה ב- TEE + ממצאים ווסקולרים
RHEUMATIOD FACTOR חיובי + Roth’s spots
keySource: IMA 2024-Sep Basic official answer key after appeals, Q106
explanation:
The Duke criteria combine microbiologic, imaging and clinical findings. Fever and a single viridans-positive blood culture supply two minor criteria. **A characteristic TEE lesion plus a vascular phenomenon** adds one major and a third minor criterion for definite endocarditis.

**A. TEE lesion alone.** This gives one major and two documented minor criteria. A new murmur alone does not prove new valve regurgitation.
**B. Existing findings suffice.** One culture set does not meet the major typical-organism criterion, and TTE has shown no qualifying lesion.
**C. TEE lesion plus vascular finding.** This fulfills the one-major, three-minor route to definite disease.
**D. Rheumatoid factor and Roth spots.** Both fall in the same immunologic category and cannot count as two separate minor criteria.

Reference · Harrison 22e, pp. 1039–1040.

Renal Tubular Acydosis Type I
Hypoaldosteronism
הרעלת סליצילטים
keySource: IMA 2024-Sep Basic official answer key after appeals, Q107
explanation:
The chemistry gives an anion gap of 10 mEq/L and potassium 5.8 mmol/L. **Hypoaldosteronism can account for hyperkalemia with low bicarbonate and a normal gap.** Confirm the data: PCO₂ 32 mmHg and bicarbonate 18 correspond to pH about 7.37 rather than the printed 7.26. The apparent biochemical pattern is more secure than the stated degree of acidemia.

**A. Diarrhea.** Gastrointestinal bicarbonate loss can cause normal-gap acidosis but usually also causes potassium loss.
**B. Distal type 1 RTA.** Impaired urinary acidification in classic type 1 RTA is generally accompanied by low potassium.
**C. Hypoaldosteronism.** Aldosterone deficiency or resistance produces an impaired renal potassium and ammonium response. Review renal function and drug exposures.
**D. Salicylate poisoning.** It more characteristically combines respiratory alkalosis with an elevated-gap metabolic acidosis.

Reference · Harrison 22e, pp. 368, 370, 372.

בת 70, מועמדת לביצוע קולונוסקופיה לבירור אנמיה ודם סמוי חיובי. ברקע מחלת לב איסכמית, אי ספיקת לב, היצרות קשה של מסתם אאורטלי לאחר TAVI, ידוע על רגישות לפניצילין.
מהי הגישה למניעת אנדוקרדיטיס במטופלת זו?
o: PO Clindamycin
PO Azytromycin
IV Ceftriaxone
אין התוויה לטיפול מניעתי
keySource: IMA 2024-Sep Basic official answer key after appeals, Q108
explanation:
A transcatheter prosthetic valve is a high-risk cardiac condition, but endocarditis prophylaxis also depends on the procedure. **Routine colonoscopy without active infection does not warrant prophylaxis** in the framework used here.

**A. Oral clindamycin.** There is no procedure-based indication, and clindamycin is no longer a favored prophylactic alternative.
**B. Oral azithromycin.** An alternative for indicated dental prophylaxis does not create an indication for colonoscopy.
**C. IV ceftriaxone.** A parenteral route does not change which procedures qualify.
**D. No prophylaxis.** Manage any separate active infection on its own merits, without routine endocarditis prophylaxis for this examination.

Reference · Harrison 22e, p. 1048.

q: מה מהממצאים הבאים אופייני לתסמונת Takotsubo ?
o: ירידה במוטיליות הקיר הקדמי של הלב באקו לב
הרמות ST באק"ג
רמות תקינות של טרופונין בדם
חסימה של כלי דם בצנתור
chapterTitle: Harrison 22e ch. 316 – Cardiogenic Shock and Pulmonary Edema
keySource: IMA 2024-Sep Basic official answer key after appeals, Q109
explanation:
Takotsubo syndrome causes transient regional ventricular dysfunction and can resemble acute MI. **ST elevation is a recognized acute finding.** A typical apical pattern involves multiple apical or midventricular segments and usually extends beyond the territory of a single coronary artery.

**A. Reduced anterior-wall motion.** Anterior segments can be hypokinetic as part of apical ballooning. This finding in isolation is nonspecific, and the option does not describe the broader distribution that distinguishes the syndrome.
**B. ST elevation.** Evaluate urgently for acute coronary occlusion because the ECG appearance can overlap.
**C. Normal troponin.** Troponin commonly rises, though the degree of elevation is often modest relative to the ventricular dysfunction.
**D. Obstruction on angiography.** A culprit occlusion explaining the full wall-motion pattern suggests MI. Coronary disease can nevertheless coexist with Takotsubo.

Reference · Harrison 22e, pp. 2019, 2331. International Expert Consensus Document on Takotsubo Syndrome, Part I, 2018.

q:
לבת 75 בוצעה בדיקת אק"ג המופיעה בתמונה מספר 7
מה מהמצבים הבאים יכול לגרום לכך?

טיפול ב- Citalopram

Thyrotoxicosis
ref: Harrison · ch. 240 · p. 1830 · Hazzard 8e · ch. 60 · p. 929; Image 7
keySource: IMA 2024-Sep Basic official answer key after appeals, Q110
explanation:
The QT interval extends from the start of the QRS complex to the end of the T wave. Prolonged repolarization on the tracing raises concern for a medication effect and susceptibility to torsades de pointes.

**Citalopram can cause dose-dependent QT prolongation.**

**A. Hypercalcemia** Raised calcium usually shortens the ST segment and QT interval.
**B. Citalopram** Its QT-prolonging effect is why dosing and interacting drugs matter in older adults.
**C. Digoxin** A typical therapeutic digitalis effect includes scooped ST depression and a shorter QT interval.
**D. Thyrotoxicosis** Sinus tachycardia and atrial fibrillation are more characteristic findings than the repolarization pattern tested here.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 929, Table 60-9; Harrison 21e, Chapter 240, p. 1830; September 2024 basic examination, image 7

q: באיזה מהמצבים הבאים נמצא PULSUS PARADOXUS?
o: אוטם קדמי נרחב
תת תזונה
COPD קשה
אי ספיקת לב
chapterTitle: Harrison 22e ch. 295 – Approach to the Patient with Disease of the Respiratory System
keySource: IMA 2024-Sep Basic official answer key after appeals, Q111
explanation:
Pulsus paradoxus is an exaggerated inspiratory fall in systolic pressure. **Severe COPD** can produce it through large intrathoracic pressure swings and altered ventricular filling during inspiration.

**A. Large anterior MI.** An infarction alone does not imply the respiratory filling disturbance. A complication such as tamponade would change the assessment.
**B. Malnutrition.** Nutritional deficiency itself is not a characteristic cause of an exaggerated inspiratory pressure fall.
**C. Severe obstructive lung disease.** Large inspiratory pressure changes can sharply reduce left ventricular filling and systolic pressure.
**D. Heart failure generally.** The broad diagnosis is less specific than severe obstruction or tamponade for this respiratory sign.

Reference · Harrison 22e, pp. 2200, 1863.

q:
בן 76, פנה למיון עקב שלשול דמי, מלווה בכאבי בטן וחום 38. מאנמנזה ידוע על ארוחה משפחתית לפני יומיים.
מה הגורם לשלשול?
o: Staph Aureus
Rotavirus
E.Coli
Clostridium Perfringens
keySource: IMA 2024-Sep Basic official answer key after appeals, Q112
explanation:
Bloody diarrhea with abdominal pain and fever suggests inflammatory enteritis. **A diarrheagenic strain of E. coli** is the best fit among the listed organisms. The clinical history alone cannot determine the exact strain.

**A. Staphylococcus aureus.** Preformed staphylococcal toxin typically causes abrupt nausea and vomiting, often within hours of eating.
**B. Rotavirus.** Rotavirus typically produces watery rather than inflammatory bloody diarrhea.
**C. E. coli.** Certain E. coli strains cause bloody colitis. Further testing may be needed before choosing treatment.
**D. Clostridium perfringens.** C. perfringens food poisoning typically causes cramps and watery diarrhea, usually without prominent fever or blood.

Reference · Harrison 22e, pp. 305–306.

q:
בן 89, אושפז עקב אי ספיקה כלייתית חדה עם עליית קראטינין מ- 0.8 ל- 2.5. בבדיקת משקע שתן נמצאו GRANULAR CASTS.
מהי האבחנה המתאימה?
o: חסימה על רקע הגדלה שפירה של הערמונית
טרומבוזיס של ה- Renal Artery
Malignant Hypertension
Acute Tubular Necrosis
keySource: IMA 2024-Sep Basic official answer key after appeals, Q113
explanation:
Pigmented granular casts arise from injured tubular cells and debris in the nephron. With a rapid creatinine rise, **acute tubular injury or necrosis** is the best fit.

**A. Prostatic obstruction.** Obstruction is evaluated through retention or hydronephrosis. Granular casts more directly implicate tubules.
**B. Renal artery thrombosis.** Vascular occlusion has a different clinical pattern and is not specifically identified by this sediment.
**C. Malignant hypertension.** Assess for severe hypertension and end-organ or microangiopathic injury. Granular casts alone do not identify that syndrome.
**D. Acute tubular necrosis.** Granular or tubular epithelial casts support structural tubular injury, though sediment is not perfectly specific.

Reference · Harrison 22e, pp. 2379–2381.

q: מה מהבאים מהווה את הסיבוך המאוחר ביותר של אוטם שריר הלב?
o: Left Ventricular Aneurysm
Ventricular Tachycardia
Papillary Muscle Rupture
Pericarditis
chapterTitle: Harrison 22e ch. 286 – ST-Segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction
keySource: IMA 2024-Sep Basic official answer key after appeals, Q114
explanation:
A true LV aneurysm develops as an infarcted wall scars and remodels. **Left ventricular aneurysm is characteristically a late complication**, often becoming clinically important weeks to months after STEMI.

**A. LV aneurysm.** A scarred, dyskinetic segment can lead to heart failure, thrombus or ventricular arrhythmia.
**B. Ventricular tachycardia.** It can develop during acute ischemia, although scar-related VT can also occur later.
**C. Papillary muscle rupture.** This mechanical complication usually presents within days, often with abrupt severe mitral regurgitation.
**D. Pericarditis.** Early infarct-associated pericarditis can occur within days. Delayed immune-mediated pericarditis is a distinct possibility.

Reference · Harrison 22e, pp. 2122–2125.

q:
בן 75, מאושפז במחלקת שיקום אחרי אוטם שריר הלב וירידה תפקודית. במהלך טיפול פיזיותרפי איבד הכרה.
בבדיקה – מחוסר הכרה, לא נושם, דופק לא נמוש. הותחל בהחייאה.
בדפיברילטור ממצאי התרשים המופיע בתמונה מספר 8.
קיבל פעמיים טיפול שוק חשמלי (דפיברילציה) ללא הטבה.
מה הטיפול התרופתי המומלץ בנוסף ל- Adrenaline?
o: Atropine
Magnesium
Amiodarone (Procor)
Adenosine
chapterTitle: Harrison 22e ch. 317 – Cardiovascular Collapse, Cardiac Arrest, and Sudden Cardiac Death
keySource: IMA 2024-Sep Basic official answer key after appeals, Q115
explanation:
Persistent pulseless VT or VF requires repeated defibrillation with immediate high-quality CPR after each shock. **Amiodarone is the listed antiarrhythmic for shock-refractory arrest. In the AHA sequence, give epinephrine during CPR after shock two and consider amiodarone or lidocaine after shock three.**

**A. Atropine.** It treats selected symptomatic bradycardia with a pulse, not refractory shockable arrest.
**B. Magnesium.** Consider it specifically for torsades de pointes associated with prolonged QT, not routinely for pulseless VT.
**C. Amiodarone.** With two shocks already delivered, continue CPR, assess the rhythm at the next check and shock again if indicated. Give the antiarrhythmic during CPR after that third shock, without delaying defibrillation.
**D. Adenosine.** It is used for selected regular tachycardias with a pulse, not routine treatment of pulseless VT.

Reference · AHA Adult Cardiac Arrest Algorithm, 2025, shockable pathway. Harrison 22e, pp. 1933, 2337.

q: איזה מהבאים מתאר נכון קשר בין תרופה לטיפול בסרטן לבין תופעת לוואי שכיחה שלה?
o: Doxorubicin (Adriamycin) – פגיעה לבבית
Cisplatin - היפרקלצמיה
5 Fluoro-Uracyl - נוירופתיה פריפרית
Rituximab - טרומבוציטופניה
chapterTitle: Harrison 22e ch. 78 – Principles of Cancer Treatment
keySource: IMA 2024-Sep Basic official answer key after appeals, Q116
explanation:
Anticancer drugs have characteristic toxicities that reflect the tissues they injure. **Doxorubicin can damage the heart**, with cumulative exposure increasing the risk of ventricular dysfunction.

**A. Doxorubicin and cardiac injury.** Anthracycline cardiotoxicity can present with arrhythmias or later cardiomyopathy.
**B. Cisplatin and hypercalcemia.** Nephrotoxicity, magnesium wasting, neuropathy and ototoxicity are more characteristic associations.
**C. 5-fluorouracil and peripheral neuropathy.** Mucositis, diarrhea and myelosuppression are more characteristic. Peripheral neuropathy is especially associated with agents such as oxaliplatin.
**D. Rituximab and thrombocytopenia.** Infusion reactions and B-cell depletion are characteristic. Thrombocytopenia is not the characteristic pairing sought here.

Reference · Harrison 22e, pp. 558, 562–565.

q: בן 70, הופנה למיון לבירור עצירות וכאבי בטן דיפוזיים מזה מספר ימים. בבירור כעת עדות קלינית ומעבדתית לחסימת מעי דק. מה מהבאים הינו הגורם השכיח ביותר לאבחנה זו?
o: הידבקויות
ממאירות
מחלת קרוהן
טיפול קרינתי לבטן בעברו
chapterTitle: Harrison 22e ch. 332 – Approach to the Patient with Gastrointestinal Disease
keySource: IMA 2024-Sep Basic official answer key after appeals, Q117
explanation:
Mechanical small-bowel obstruction prevents intestinal contents passing an obstructed segment. **Adhesions**, often from previous abdominal surgery, are the commonest cause among the choices.

**A. Adhesions.** Fibrous bands can kink or tether a mobile loop of small bowel.
**B. Malignancy.** Cancer can obstruct the small bowel but is particularly important in large-bowel obstruction.
**C. Crohn disease.** Inflammatory or fibrotic strictures can obstruct, especially with an established history of Crohn disease.
**D. Previous radiotherapy.** Radiation enteritis can produce strictures, but it is a less common overall cause.

Reference · Harrison 22e, p. 2459.

q: באיזו מהמחלות הזיהומיות הבאות מומלץ להתחיל טיפול אמפירי ב- Ceftriaxone + Vancomycin?
o: Bacterial Meningitis
Septic Shock
Hospital Acquired Pneumonia
Necrotizing Fasciitis
chapterTitle: Harrison 22e ch. 127 – Approach to the Acutely Ill Infected Febrile Patient
keySource: IMA 2024-Sep Basic official answer key after appeals, Q118
explanation:
Ceftriaxone plus vancomycin is an empiric backbone for **community-acquired bacterial meningitis**, pending microbiologic results. Add ampicillin when Listeria risk, including older age, is present.

**A. Bacterial meningitis.** The combination covers common meningeal pathogens and resistant pneumococci.
**B. Septic shock.** Initial coverage depends on likely focus, setting and resistance risk, often requiring broader gram-negative activity.
**C. Hospital-acquired pneumonia.** Ceftriaxone does not provide reliable antipseudomonal coverage needed in many hospital-acquired cases.
**D. Necrotizing fasciitis.** Urgent surgery and broad coverage of aerobic and anaerobic organisms are needed, with toxin-directed therapy when indicated.

Reference · Harrison 22e, pp. 990–991, 1175.

q:
בת 72 מדווחת על נטיה מולדת לדמם בפעולות פולשניות ולידות. ללא דימומים ספונטנים.

o: חסר פקטור VII
לופוס אנטי קואגולנט
חסר פקטור VIII
גלנצמן טרומבסטניה
keySource: IMA 2024-Sep Basic official answer key after appeals, Q119
explanation:
Factor VII participates in the extrinsic pathway assessed by PT. **Factor VII deficiency** fits a prolonged PT and INR with a normal aPTT and platelet count.

**A. Factor VII deficiency.** An isolated factor VII defect can prolong PT while leaving the intrinsic pathway assay normal.
**B. Lupus anticoagulant.** A lupus anticoagulant more often prolongs a phospholipid-dependent aPTT assay.
**C. Factor VIII deficiency.** Factor VIII deficiency affects the intrinsic pathway and typically prolongs aPTT.
**D. Glanzmann thrombasthenia.** Glanzmann thrombasthenia impairs platelet aggregation and usually leaves both PT and aPTT normal.

Reference · Harrison 22e, pp. 472, 474–475.

q:
בן 75, ברקע ידוע על יתר לחץ דם, אי ספיקת לב, אלכוהוליזם. אושפז לבירור ירידה בתיאבון, ירידה במשקל והופעה של מיימת חדשה. כחלק מהבירור בוצע ניקור מיימת.
מה נכון לומר לגבי המדדים מנוזל המיימת?
o: במידה ומדובר בטרנסודט, קרוב לוודאי מדובר במיימת על רקע אי ספיקת לב
במידה ו- SAAG (Serum Ascites-to-Albumin Gradient) מעל 1.1 g/dL, קרוב לוודאי מדובר ביתר לחץ דם פורטלי
מיימת על רקע אי ספיקת לב (Cardiac Ascites) מאופיינת על ידי רמת חלבון מתחת ל 2.5 g/dL בנוזל המיימת
רמת החלבון בנוזל המיימת מעל 1.5 g/dL מעלה סיכון לפתח SBP (Spontaneous Bacterial Peritonitis)
chapterTitle: Harrison 22e ch. 355 – Cirrhosis and Its Complications
keySource: IMA 2024-Sep Basic official answer key after appeals, Q120
explanation:
The serum–ascites albumin gradient (SAAG) estimates whether increased portal pressure drives fluid accumulation. **A SAAG of at least 1.1 g/dL supports portal hypertension**. Total ascitic protein helps distinguish causes within that group.

**A. A transudate means heart failure.** Older transudate terminology does not specifically identify cardiac ascites.
**B. High SAAG indicates portal hypertension.** Both cirrhosis and congestive heart failure can generate this gradient.
**C. Cardiac ascites has low total protein.** Cardiac ascites usually combines a high SAAG with total protein of at least 2.5 g/dL.
**D. Higher protein raises SBP risk.** Low ascitic protein, rather than a level above 1.5 g/dL, helps identify selected higher-risk patients.

Reference · Harrison 22e, p. 2715.

q: מה מהבאים אופייני למעורבות הפריקרד בחולים אונקולוגיים?
o: מתייצג לעיתים קרובות כטמפונדה
ברוב החולים האונקולוגיים עם פריקרדיטיס נמצא תאים ממאירים בניקור הנוזל
מדידת מרקרים בנוזל לא מסייעת באבחון הנוזל כממאיר
מגיב טוב לטיפול בסטרואידים
keySource: IMA 2024-Sep Basic official answer key after appeals, Q121
explanation:
Cancer-associated pericardial disease can result from malignancy, radiation, drugs or other illnesses. **Fluid cytology can identify malignant cells in malignant effusions, while fluid tumor markers are generally unhelpful**. The denominator matters.

**A. Often presents as tamponade.** Effusions may be asymptomatic. Tamponade can occur but is not the usual presentation of every cancer-associated effusion.
**B. Malignant cells in most cancer patients with pericarditis.** Cytologic yield can be high in malignant effusions. Extending that statement to every cancer patient with pericarditis includes many nonmalignant cases.
**C. Fluid tumor markers are unhelpful.** Routine marker levels do not reliably distinguish malignant fluid. Examine cytology and consider tissue sampling when needed.
**D. Good steroid response.** Treatment depends on cause. A malignant effusion may need drainage and tumor-directed therapy.

Reference · Harrison 22e, p. 587.
Key note: Harrison says about half of symptomatic pericardial disease in patients with cancer is nonmalignant. Cytology is useful in malignant effusions, but the exam also credits a statement applying malignant cells to most cancer patients with pericarditis.

q:
בן 67, ללא עבר של עישון ופעיל גופנית, מגיע למרפאה עם תלונה על שיעול יבש קוצר נשימה מזה שישה חודשים. בבדיקה יש קרפיטציות אינספירטוריות בבסיסי שתי הריאות ו- Clubbing באצבעות.
בבדיקת תפקודי ריאה יש ירידה ב- FEV1, TLC ו- FVC ביחס לנורמה וירידה בדיפוזיה (DLCO).
אילו ממצאים נוספים צפויים להיות?
o: בבדיקת High resolution CT נראה תמונה של "חלת דבש"
בבדיקת אקו לב נראה ירידה בתפקוד הסיסטולי
בצילום חזה נראה סימנים של לימפאדנופתיה בשערי הריאה
בבדיקת CT נראה אמפיזמה משמעותית
keySource: IMA 2024-Sep Basic official answer key after appeals, Q122
explanation:
Progressive dry cough, basal inspiratory crackles, clubbing, restriction and low DLCO suggest fibrotic interstitial lung disease. **Basal subpleural honeycombing on high-resolution CT** supports a usual interstitial pneumonia pattern, compatible with IPF after other causes are excluded.

**A. Honeycombing.** Subpleural basal reticulation, traction bronchiectasis and honeycomb cysts are characteristic CT features.
**B. Reduced LV systolic function.** Cardiac failure can cause dyspnea and crackles but does not explain clubbing and the expected fibrotic pattern.
**C. Hilar lymphadenopathy.** This is more suggestive of sarcoidosis than the usual IPF presentation.
**D. Marked emphysema.** It can reduce gas transfer, but emphysema alone usually does not produce restrictive volumes and typical basal fibrotic changes.

Reference · Harrison 22e, pp. 2260, 2262.

q:
בן 74 הגיע למרפאה עקב בצקות מפושטות. המטופל ללא מחלות רקע ידועות ולא עשה בדיקות דם בשנים האחרונות.
איזה ממצא בבדיקה גופנית מכוון לגורם אפשרי לבצקות?
o: עליה ב- JVP מכוונת לשחמת
ממצא של קריפיטציות בריאות מכוון לאי ספיקת כליות
בצקות פריאורביטליות מכוונות להיפואלבומינמיה
PULSE PRESSURE גבוה מכוון לאי ספיקת לב
keySource: IMA 2024-Sep Basic official answer key after appeals, Q123
explanation:
Low plasma albumin reduces oncotic pressure and permits fluid to move into tissue. **Periorbital edema can point toward hypoalbuminemia**, particularly in renal protein loss. The finding prompts evaluation rather than proving its cause.

**A. Raised JVP points to cirrhosis.** Raised JVP indicates elevated systemic venous pressure and favors cardiac congestion over uncomplicated cirrhosis.
**B. Pulmonary crackles point to renal failure.** Crackles suggest lung fluid or parenchymal disease. They are not specific for kidney failure.
**C. Periorbital edema points to hypoalbuminemia.** Loose periorbital tissue can show edema when serum oncotic pressure is low. Check albumin and urine protein.
**D. High pulse pressure points to heart failure.** A wide pulse pressure is nonspecific and is not the characteristic sign of heart-failure edema.

Reference · Harrison 22e, p. 281.

q: בת 72, פליטה מאוקראינה, ללא היסטוריה רפואית ידועה, לדבריה בריאה בדרך כלל, לא שותה הרבה אלכוהול, וללא טיפול תרופתי קבוע. הופנתה בשל הרגשה כללית רעה מזה 2-3 ימים. בבדיקות הדם הפרעה משולבת באנזימי כבד. אילו מהממצאים הבאים מכוונים לכך שמדובר בהפרעה ממושכת, ולא אקוטית?
o: רמת ALT גבוהה יותר מאשר AST.
הפרעה בתפקודי קרישה
רמה תקינה של אמוניה
רמת אלבומין מתחת ל 3 gr/dL
chapterTitle: Harrison 22e ch. 348 – Evaluation of Liver Function
keySource: IMA 2024-Sep Basic official answer key after appeals, Q124
explanation:
Albumin is synthesized by the liver and turns over over several weeks. **An albumin below 3 g/dL is a clue to pre-existing liver disease** when the apparent illness is only two days old. Other causes of hypoalbuminemia still need consideration.

**A. ALT above AST.** This ratio can occur in acute hepatocellular injury and does not date the process.
**B. Abnormal coagulation.** Short-lived clotting factors can fall rapidly in severe acute hepatic failure.
**C. Normal ammonia.** Ammonia is an unreliable measure of chronicity and does not exclude significant liver disease.
**D. Marked hypoalbuminemia.** Slow turnover makes a major fall less likely to be explained by a brief isolated hepatic insult.

Reference · Harrison 22e, pp. 2635–2637.

q:
בן 82, לא ידוע על ירידה קוגניטיבית, ברקע ידוע על שחמת מזה כ- 20 שנים, על רקע כבד שומני.
אושפז בשל מספר הקאות דמיות כשעתיים טרם קבלתו, מלווה בדליריום. לציין 3-4 אירועים דומים בשנים האחרונות, אירוע אחרון לפני שנה וחצי, אז עבר קשירת דליות. בקבלתו יציב המודינמית ונשימתית, חום סיסטמי תקין. בבדיקות דם ללא חריגות משמעותיות ביחס לבדיקות קודמות, למעט רמת HB 10, כאשר הבסיס סביב 11, מה נכון לומר לגבי הבירור והטיפול במצבו?
o: המטופל מתאים לחוק החולה הנוטה למות, יש לבדוק אם קיימות הנחיות מקדימות, ולשקול להימנע מטיפולים פולשניים בהתאם
מתן מנת דם, ובמידה וההמוגלובין יישאר יציב עד הבוקר למחרת ויהיה שיפור במצבו הקוגניטיבי, תבוצע גסטרוסקופיה אבחנתית
לנוכח סיכון של 20-30% לתמותה סביב כל אירוע של דימום מדליות, חשוב ליידע את אישתו של המטופל על מצבו, ולהקפיד על מעקב קליני ומעבדתי קפדני
בהיעדר מדדי דלקת מוגברים, ולנוכח חשד נמוך ל- SBP (Spontaneous Bacterial Peritonitis), אין מקום למתן טיפול אנטיביוטי
chapterTitle: Harrison 22e ch. 355 – Cirrhosis and Its Complications
keySource: IMA 2024-Sep Basic official answer key after appeals, Q125
explanation:
Recurrent hematemesis in cirrhosis with previous variceal bleeding is a potentially fatal emergency even when blood pressure is initially stable. **Communicate the risk and monitor closely while starting a vasoactive agent and antibiotic prophylaxis immediately. Arrange therapeutic endoscopy after stabilization, generally within 12 hours.**

**A. Assume he is a dying patient.** Cirrhosis and delirium alone do not meet the statutory definition or justify withholding urgent treatment.
**B. Transfuse and wait until tomorrow.** Hemoglobin near 10 g/dL in a stable patient does not automatically require blood. Airway, circulation and timely therapeutic endoscopy take priority over waiting for delirium to resolve.
**C. Inform family and monitor.** Explain the substantial mortality risk, assess ability to participate and share appropriate information. Monitoring must accompany vasoactive therapy such as octreotide or terlipressin and endoscopic hemostasis.
**D. Omit antibiotics because inflammation is absent.** Acute upper GI bleeding in cirrhosis warrants infection prophylaxis, commonly ceftriaxone, independently of a diagnosis of SBP.

Reference · Harrison 22e, pp. 2713–2714. Baveno VII consensus, acute variceal bleeding.

q: מה אופייני לאפידמיולוגיה הזיהומית במטופלים לאחר כריתת טחול?

הסיכון לזיהומים גבוה יותר בשלוש השנים הראשונות לאחר הניתוח
סיכון מוגבר לזיהומים בחיידקים גרהם שליליים
כ- 3-5% מהמטופלים יפתחו זיהום מסכן חיים במהלך חייהם
chapterTitle: Harrison 22e ch. 70 – Enlargement of Lymph Nodes and Spleen
keySource: IMA 2024-Sep Basic official answer key after appeals, Q126
explanation:
Loss of splenic filtration increases the risk of invasive bacterial infection, especially from encapsulated organisms. **Risk is highest in the first three years and remains lifelong; it includes selected gram-negative bacteria.** Estimates depend on whether the outcome is fulminant postsplenectomy infection, sepsis or any serious infection.

**A. Increased viral infections.** The characteristic excess is for invasive bacterial infections. Splenectomy alone does not produce generalized viral susceptibility.
**B. First three years.** Infection occurs most frequently early after splenectomy, although severe illness can develop decades later.
**C. Gram-negative infections.** Haemophilus influenzae and other selected gram-negative organisms are relevant alongside pneumococcus.
**D. Lifetime life-threatening infection of 3% to 5%.** An estimate near 5% has been reported for specifically defined overwhelming postsplenectomy infection. Separate estimates of about 7% for sepsis over ten years and 25% for lifetime serious infection measure different outcomes.

Reference · Harrison 22e, p. 482. Prevention and management of infections in patients without a spleen, PMID 11843905.
Key note: A lifetime risk near 5% is compatible with estimates for fulminant OPSI. It cannot be compared directly with ten-year sepsis or broader lifetime serious-infection estimates.

q:
בת 80, פנתה לבירור בשל חולשה גוברת. במעבדה Hb = 8.1, רמת ויטמין B12 = 100.
מה מהבאים מתאים לאבחנה של חסר ויטמין B12?
o: Reticulocyte index = 1.1
MCV=90
LDH מוגבר
תאי מטרה במשטח דם
keySource: IMA 2024-Sep Basic official answer key after appeals, Q127
explanation:
Vitamin B12 deficiency causes ineffective erythropoiesis, with destruction of precursors in the marrow. **A low reticulocyte index despite anemia and an elevated LDH** both fit this process.

**A. Reticulocyte index 1.1.** An index of 1.1 is inappropriately low for hemoglobin of 8.1, supporting inadequate marrow output.
**B. MCV 90.** An MCV of 90 can occur with a mixed disorder, but macrocytosis is the classic clue to isolated B12 deficiency.
**C. Raised LDH.** Intramedullary breakdown releases LDH, sometimes causing a marked elevation.
**D. Target cells.** Target cells more often suggest liver disease or a hemoglobin disorder. Macro-ovalocytes and hypersegmented neutrophils are the characteristic megaloblastic findings.

Reference · Harrison 22e, pp. 437, 449–450, 784–785.

q: מה מהבאים נכון לגבי פגיעה כלייתית מאמינוגליקוזידים?
o: מאופיינת בהיפרמגנזמיה בבדיקות הדם
יכולה להופיע גם שבוע לאחר סיום הטיפול
תלויה ברמת התרופה בדם
נגרמת כתוצאה מנזק לגלומרולים
keySource: IMA 2024-Sep Basic official answer key after appeals, Q128
explanation:
Aminoglycosides accumulate in proximal tubular cells and can cause delayed, often nonoliguric AKI. **Creatinine may rise after the last dose**, because serum creatinine lags behind injury and renal tissue exposure can persist. It need not appear at exactly one week.

**A. Hypermagnesemia.** Tubular injury can cause magnesium wasting and hypomagnesemia, rather than a characteristic rise in magnesium.
**B. Delayed kidney injury.** Follow renal function after a prolonged or high-risk course even if creatinine was initially stable.
**C. Risk depends on serum concentrations.** This is partly correct. High or sustained trough exposure increases risk, along with duration, baseline renal function and other nephrotoxins. A single therapeutic level does not exclude injury.
**D. Glomerular injury.** Filtration delivers the drug to the nephron, but the characteristic cellular injury is predominantly proximal tubular.

Reference · Harrison 21e, p. 2300. KDIGO AKI guideline, aminoglycoside therapeutic drug monitoring.
Key note: Higher or sustained serum exposure contributes to aminoglycoside nephrotoxicity. The concentration-dependent risk statement is defensible without treating any one level as conclusive.
referenceNote: Explanation read from Harrison 21e; official reference retained as printed.

q: מה ניתן למצוא בהאזנה במטופל עם איוושה סיסטולית שבאקו לב ממצאים המתאימים ל- Hypertrophic Obstructive Cardiomyopathy?
o: האיוושה תשמע מקסימלית במרווח בין צלעי שני מימין
האיוושה תתגבר בעת הרמת רגלי המטופל
האיוושה תהיה מיד-סיסטולית
תשמע איוושה דיאסטולית אפיקלית נילוות (Austin Flint Murmur)
keySource: IMA 2024-Sep Basic official answer key after appeals, Q129
explanation:
Hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy produces dynamic left ventricular outflow obstruction. Its **midsystolic ejection murmur**, often harsh and late-peaking, becomes louder when ventricular filling decreases.

**A. Loudest in the second right interspace.** The second right interspace is the classic site for aortic stenosis; the obstructive cardiomyopathy murmur is usually prominent along the left sternal border or apex.
**B. Louder with passive leg elevation.** Passive leg raising increases preload and generally reduces dynamic obstruction.
**C. Midsystolic murmur.** Ejection through the dynamically narrowed outflow tract produces this systolic murmur.
**D. Associated Austin Flint murmur.** An Austin Flint murmur is an apical diastolic finding of significant aortic regurgitation.

Reference · Harrison 22e, pp. 1865–1867, 2006.

q:
בן 75 עובר בדיקה במעבדת שינה בשל תלונות על נחירות, הפסקות נשימה ליליות ועייפות ונמנום במשך היום.
בבדיקה נמצא AHI of ≥30 events/h.
מה נכון לגבי הטיפול?
o: טיפול ב-CPAP אינו מוכח כיעיל בטיפול במצבו
שיעור ההיענות לשימוש בסדים מנדיבולריים נמוך יותר ביחס ל-CPAP
גודש באף היא תופעת לוואי של טיפול ב- CPAP
טיפול ניתוחי בדרכי האויר העליונות יעיל יותר מ-CPAP בטיפול במצבו
keySource: IMA 2024-Sep Basic official answer key after appeals, Q130
explanation:
CPAP splints the upper airway open during sleep and can relieve obstructive events and daytime sleepiness. **Nasal congestion is a recognized adverse effect of CPAP** and can affect adherence.

**A. CPAP lacks efficacy.** Symptomatic severe obstructive sleep apnea is a setting where CPAP is effective when used.
**B. Mandibular devices have poorer adherence.** Adherence and physiological efficacy are distinct. Some patients tolerate oral appliances better, even when CPAP controls events more completely.
**C. Nasal congestion.** Mask fit, humidification and management of nasal symptoms can help patients continue therapy.
**D. Upper-airway surgery is more effective.** Surgery helps selected anatomy but is not generally superior to adequately used CPAP.

Reference · Harrison 22e, p. 2281.

q: מה ההבדל בסיבוכים בין החלפת מסתם אאורטלי בניתוח לבין TAVI?
o: שיעור התפתחות פרפור עליות גבוה יותר לאחר TAVI לעומת ניתוח
שיעור היארעות שבץ מוחי גבוה יותר אחרי TAVI לעומת ניתוח
צורך בהשתלת קוצב לב באחוז יותר גבוה לאחר TAVI לעומת ניתוח
דלף סביב המסתם (PARAVALVULAR LEAK) בשכיחות נמוכה יותר לאחר TAVI לעומת ניתוח
keySource: IMA 2024-Sep Basic official answer key after appeals, Q131
explanation:
Transcatheter aortic valve implantation seats a prosthesis inside the diseased valve. Its proximity to the conduction system helps explain one important difference in complications from open surgical replacement.
**A permanent pacemaker is needed more often after transcatheter implantation than after surgery.**

**A. More atrial fibrillation with TAVI.** In the comparisons described, new postoperative atrial fibrillation was more frequent with open surgery.
**B. More stroke with TAVI.** In the valve-replacement trials considered here, TAVI had lower postoperative stroke rates than open surgery. The comparison with medical management in inoperable patients is a different question.
**C. More permanent pacing with TAVI.** Implantation can injure the conduction system near the aortic annulus. Persistent conduction block can require pacing.
**D. Less paravalvular leak with TAVI.** An imperfect seal between the implanted valve and the calcified annulus can leave a leak. These leaks were more frequent after TAVI.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 1152–1153, transcatheter aortic valve replacement and Table 75-3.

q:
בת 80, אושפזה לבירור אנמיה מחסר ברזל. ברקע דיסליפידמיה ויתר לחץ דם, מטופלת ב- ASPIRIN למניעה ראשונית. בגסטרוסקופיה הודגם כיב בתוכו כלי דם מדמם, בוצעה צריבה והונחו קליפסים. ביופסיה חזרה חיובית להימצאות של Helicobacter Pylori. הותחל טיפול במעכבי משאבת פרוטונים (PPI – Proton Pump Inhibitors), והומלץ על השלמת קורס אנטיביוטי.
מה ההמלצות למטופלת זו?
o: לאירדיקציה מלאה של Helicobacter Pylori יש ליטול טיפול אנטיביוטי רציף במשך 4 שבועות
מומלץ לחדש את הטיפול באספירין תוך שבוע
טיפול במעכבי משאבות פרוטונים (PPI) לשארית חייה
לאחר האנדוסקופיה, יכולה לשתות נוזלים בלבד למשך 48 שעות
keySource: IMA 2024-Sep Basic official answer key after appeals, Q132
explanation:
An actively bleeding ulcer treated with clips and cautery remains at higher early rebleeding risk than a clean-based ulcer. **Initially use clear liquids if stable and advance intake according to hemostasis, rebleeding risk and the endoscopic team's plan.** A 48-hour period is one conservative option, not a universal requirement.

**A. Four weeks of uninterrupted eradication antibiotics.** Standard H. pylori regimens are shorter, typically 14 days with an appropriate current regimen. Confirm eradication afterward.
**B. Restart aspirin within a week.** She used aspirin for primary prevention. Reassess its indication after this major bleed, unlike aspirin needed for secondary cardiovascular prevention.
**C. Lifelong PPI.** Use appropriate high-dose post-hemostasis therapy and treat the ulcer. Long-term continuation depends on recurring risks and indications.
**D. Liquids only for 48 hours.** A short restricted period permits early monitoring and can facilitate repeat endoscopy if bleeding recurs. Once stable, the timing of diet advancement is individualized.

Reference · Harrison 22e, pp. 317, 2530–2531. Randomized study of 24- versus 48-hour feeding after hemostasis in high-risk ulcers, PMID 32205642.

q:
בן 70, ברקע סוכרת, אי ספיקת לב וממאירות ריאה גרורתית מסוג Small Cell Carcinoma.
מתאשפז לבירור השתנה מרובה. כמות שתן ביממה 3.5 ליטר. אוסמולריות השתן 200mosml/L.
מה הסיבה המתאימה לממצאים אלו?
o: Resolving Acute Tubular Necrosis
Uncontrolled Diabetes Mellitus
Hypercalcemia
High dose Furosemide (Fusid)
chapterTitle: Harrison 22e ch. 55 – Azotemia and Urinary Abnormalities
keySource: IMA 2024-Sep Basic official answer key after appeals, Q133
explanation:
Polyuria with a urine osmolality of 200 mOsm/L suggests predominantly water rather than solute diuresis. **Hypercalcemia can impair the kidney's response to vasopressin**, producing dilute urine. Verify the serum calcium rather than inferring it solely from the cancer diagnosis.

**A. Resolving ATN.** During recovery from tubular injury there can be polyuria, but the vignette does not describe a preceding oliguric or azotemic phase.
**B. Uncontrolled diabetes mellitus.** Hyperglycemia causes glucosuria and a solute diuresis, which generally raises urinary osmole excretion.
**C. Hypercalcemia.** Hypercalcemia can produce nephrogenic diabetes insipidus with inappropriately dilute urine.
**D. High-dose furosemide.** Loop diuretics can increase salt and water loss. High-dose exposure is not reported and is less directly matched to this water-diuresis pattern.

Reference · Harrison 22e, p. 343.

q: באיזה מהמקרים הבאים צפוי FeNa<1%?
o: Rhabdomyolysis
Sepsis
Contrast Nephropathy
Pre-Renal Azotemia
keySource: IMA 2024-Sep Basic official answer key after appeals, Q134
explanation:
Fractional sodium excretion (FeNa) estimates how much filtered sodium appears in urine. **A FeNa below one percent can occur in prerenal azotemia, rhabdomyolysis, early sepsis and contrast-associated injury.** A low value does not prove an exclusively prerenal process.

**A. Rhabdomyolysis.** Pigment-associated tubular injury can coexist with low fractional sodium excretion.
**B. Sepsis.** An early low value may rise later as tubular injury evolves.
**C. Contrast nephropathy.** Low FeNa can occur despite intrinsic renal injury.
**D. Prerenal azotemia.** With reduced effective perfusion and preserved tubular function, the kidney avidly retains sodium.

Reference · Harrison 22e, pp. 2379, 2381.

keySource: IMA 2024-Sep Basic official answer key after appeals, Q135
explanation:
Primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC) produces multifocal bile-duct strictures. **MR cholangiopancreatography (MRCP) can show characteristic stricturing and beading** in large-duct PSC.

**A. Hepatitis C serology because 80 percent develop cirrhosis.** Testing for HCV is reasonable, but the option confuses persistence of infection with the smaller proportion progressing to cirrhosis.
**B. AMA positive in only 20 to 40 percent of PBC.** Antimitochondrial antibodies are present in most patients with primary biliary cholangitis.
**C. MRCP for PSC.** The duct pattern can support diagnosis without using invasive cholangiography as the initial study.
**D. Echocardiography diagnoses cardiac cirrhosis.** Echo can show the cardiac disorder causing hepatic congestion. It does not by itself diagnose established cirrhosis.

Reference · Harrison 22e, pp. 2710–2712.

explanation:
Gout commonly begins at night with rapid joint inflammation. The first metatarsophalangeal joint is a classic site, but **finger, wrist and elbow involvement becomes more prominent in older patients**.

**A. Most affected women are premenopausal.** Gout in women occurs more commonly after menopause.
**B. First MTP involvement in nearly one-third.** This underestimates the prominence of podagra in the usual disease course.
**C. More upper-limb involvement in older patients.** Later-life gout may involve more joints and can present with hand or wrist disease.
**D. Equal onset throughout the day.** Flares often start overnight rather than being evenly distributed.

Reference · Harrison 22e, pp. 2956, 2958.

explanation:
Heavy proteinuria can create a prothrombotic state because regulatory proteins escape in the urine. **Loss of natural anticoagulants through the kidney** helps explain venous thromboembolism in nephrotic disease.

**A. Reduced factor III activity.** This is not the characteristic mechanism of nephrotic hypercoagulability.
**B. Urinary anticoagulant loss.** Loss of factors such as antithrombin shifts the balance toward clot formation.
**C. Abnormal platelet aggregation.** Uremic platelet dysfunction often contributes to bleeding, a separate issue in advanced CKD.
**D. Impaired prothrombin consumption.** This does not explain the link between substantial urinary protein loss and thrombosis.

Reference · Harrison 22e, p. 2393.

בן 67, מעשן 20 שנות קופסא. פונה למלר"ד בשל שיעול דמי מזה כיומיים עם החמרה בשעתיים האחרונות, מדד בערך כמות של כוס דם. בבדיקתו: סטורציה 87% באוויר חדר, מתוקנת עם 2 ליטר חמצן ל- 98%. לחץ דם 90/60, דופק 110 לדקה, סדיר.

ברונכוסקופיה קשיחה בחדר ניתוח
ניתוח לכריתת הממצא המדמם
השכבה ב- Prone Poisition
keySource: IMA 2024-Sep Basic official answer key after appeals, Q138
explanation:
With severe hemoptysis, initial priorities are airway protection, oxygenation and hemodynamic stabilization. Once the airway is protected, **bronchial-artery embolization is the preferred listed definitive bleeding-control procedure** for a bronchial arterial source.

**A. Bronchial artery embolization.** Selective occlusion of the bleeding bronchial artery can stop hemorrhage without open lung resection.
**B. Rigid bronchoscopy in the operating room.** Bronchoscopy can localize or temporarily control bleeding and support the airway, but does not replace arterial control when embolization is feasible.
**C. Immediate resection.** Immediate resection is more invasive and is generally reserved for selected or refractory causes.
**D. Prone positioning.** Prone positioning is not definitive hemorrhage control. Positioning is chosen to protect the nonbleeding lung.

Reference · Harrison 22e, pp. 275–276.

q:
בן 71, ברקע Cardiac Cirrhosis, אי ספיקת כליות עם קריאטנין בסיס סביב 2 mg/dL. מתאשפז בשל דה-קומפנסציה כבדית ומיימת קשה.

מהי הפרעת החומצה בסיס ממנה סובל המטופל?
o: Normal Anion Gap Metabolic Acidosis משולב עם Respiratory Alkalosis
Normal Anion Gap Metabolic Acidosis
High Anion Gap Metabolic Acidosis
High Anion Gap Metabolic Acidosis משולב עם Metabolic Alkalosis
keySource: IMA 2024-Sep Basic official answer key after appeals, Q139
explanation:
Albumin is a major unmeasured anion. A very low albumin can hide an increased anion gap. **High-anion-gap metabolic acidosis with appropriate respiratory compensation** fits these values after correcting for albumin.

**A. Normal-gap acidosis plus respiratory alkalosis.** PCO₂ of 37 is in the expected compensatory range of about 36 to 40 for bicarbonate 20. There is no separate respiratory alkalosis shown.
**B. Normal-gap acidosis alone.** The uncorrected gap is 10, but albumin is only 2.1. Treating this as an uncorrected normal gap misses retained unmeasured acids.
**C. High-gap metabolic acidosis.** Using albumin 4.5 as the reference, the correction adds about 6 to the measured gap, yielding approximately 16.
**D. High-gap acidosis plus metabolic alkalosis.** A separate metabolic alkalosis is not required to explain the bicarbonate and compensated PCO₂ in this vignette.

Reference · Harrison 22e, pp. 367–368.

keySource: IMA 2024-Sep Basic official answer key after appeals, Q140
explanation:
Nitroglycerin reduces venous return. In **right ventricular infarction**, maintaining preload may be essential, and nitrates can precipitate profound hypotension.

**A. Systolic pressure above 150.** Hypertension is not the pressure-related contraindication. Low blood pressure raises concern.
**B. First-degree AV block.** This conduction delay is more relevant to selected rate-slowing drugs than to nitroglycerin.
**C. Right ventricular infarction.** A damaged right ventricle may be unable to maintain left-sided filling when venous return falls.
**D. Sildenafil a week ago.** The usual nitrate exclusion interval after sildenafil is 24 hours, not a week.

Reference · Harrison 22e, p. 2109.

chapterTitle: Harrison 22e ch. 355 – Cirrhosis and Its Complications
keySource: IMA 2024-Sep Basic official answer key after appeals, Q141
explanation:
Corticosteroids may improve short-term outcomes in selected patients with severe alcohol-associated hepatitis after contraindications are addressed. **Assess response with the Lille score on day 4 or 7. A responder can complete a 28-day course**, with monitoring for infection and other adverse effects.

**A. Start for discriminant function below 30.** Lower severity alone is not an indication. The historical severe threshold is a Maddrey discriminant function of at least 32.
**B. Continue for 28 days with good response.** Continue only when early response and clinical status justify it.
**C. Present a nonresponder for transplant evaluation.** This can be appropriate for selected severe nonresponders. Evaluation is distinct from listing, which requires medical and psychosocial assessment. Homelessness or a recent drink alone does not decide candidacy.
**D. Biopsy every nonresponder.** Reserve biopsy for genuine diagnostic uncertainty. Lack of a steroid response alone does not require biopsy.

Reference · Harrison 22e, pp. 2709–2710. ACG Clinical Guideline: Alcohol-Associated Liver Disease, 2024.
Key note: Referral for early transplant evaluation is reasonable in carefully selected severe steroid nonresponders. It is not the same as automatic listing.

chapterTitle: Harrison 22e ch. 79 – Infections in Patients with Cancer
keySource: IMA 2024-Sep Basic official answer key after appeals, Q142
explanation:
Some bloodstream isolates prompt a search for an underlying malignancy. **Streptococcus bovis-group bacteremia, particularly S. gallolyticus, is associated with colorectal neoplasia** and should prompt colonic evaluation.

**A. AML and Pneumocystis.** Neutropenia in AML particularly predisposes to bacterial and fungal infection. Pneumocystis risk depends on cellular immunosuppression and treatment.
**B. Colon carcinoma and S. bovis-group bacteremia.** This is the characteristic organism–tumor association in the choices.
**C. Hodgkin disease and pneumococcus.** Pneumococcal vulnerability is especially associated with loss of splenic function or antibody deficiency, not this specific cancer–infection pairing.
**D. Myeloma and gram-negative urosepsis.** Impaired antibody production in myeloma particularly predisposes to encapsulated bacterial infection. Urosepsis is not its signature association.

Reference · Harrison 22e, pp. 577–578, 1214.

explanation:
Potassium is 2.9 mmol/L, and IV replacement requires monitoring in renal impairment. **Avoid the dextrose-containing potassium solution as the initial replacement fluid here** because glucose-induced insulin release can shift more potassium into cells.

**A. Ringer lactate.** This contains no dextrose. Its small potassium content alone should not be mistaken for adequate replacement.
**B. Normal saline with KCl 40 mEq.** Saline with KCl can provide replacement without a glucose load. Dose, rate and follow-up depend on renal function and monitoring.
**C. Half-normal saline, KCl and dextrose.** The dextrose can transiently worsen the measured hypokalemia through an intracellular shift.
**D. Half-normal saline with KCl 40 mEq.** This alternative contains KCl without dextrose. The appropriate saline concentration also depends on volume and sodium status.

Reference · Harrison 22e, p. 357.

explanation:
Calcium affects the duration of the ventricular action potential. A short QT interval together with abdominal symptoms favors **hypercalcemia**, which shortens the ST segment.

**A. Hypernatremia.** High sodium mainly causes neurologic symptoms and is not the characteristic explanation for a short QT.
**B. Hypercalcemia.** Elevated calcium shortens ventricular repolarization and can cause gastrointestinal symptoms.
**C. Hyperkalemia.** High potassium more often produces peaked T waves, PR prolongation and QRS widening as severity increases.
**D. Hyperphosphatemia.** High phosphate does not typically produce this ECG pattern and may lower calcium.

Reference · Harrison 22e, pp. 363–364, 1874–1875.

q: מה לא מהווה חלק מפרוטוקול הטיפול האקוטי בהיפרקלמיה?
o: IV NaHCO3 50 ml over 5 minutes
IV Furosemide 40 mg – push
IV Insulin 10 U - push
IV Calcium gluconate 10% 10 ml over 2-3 minutes
chapterTitle: Harrison 22e ch. 56 – Fluid and Electrolyte Disturbances
keySource: IMA 2024-Sep Basic official answer key after appeals, Q145
explanation:
Emergency hyperkalemia treatment distinguishes cardiac membrane stabilization, intracellular redistribution and potassium removal. **A rapid IV bicarbonate bolus over five minutes is not a routine rapid potassium-lowering intervention**.

**A. IV bicarbonate over five minutes.** Bicarbonate may have a role in selected acidotic patients, but its potassium effect is slower and should not replace established emergency measures.
**B. IV furosemide.** Furosemide can promote urinary potassium removal if perfusion, volume status and renal response allow.
**C. IV insulin 10 units.** Insulin rapidly shifts potassium into cells. Glucose administration and monitoring limit hypoglycemia risk.
**D. IV calcium gluconate.** IV calcium stabilizes the myocardium in dangerous hyperkalemia. It does not lower total body potassium.

Reference · Harrison 22e, p. 361.

q: איזה מהמאפיינים הבאים אינו מתאים ל- Viral Encephalitis?
o: רמות גלוקוז תקינות ב- CSF
אמפליטודות גבוהות וגלים איטיים ב- EEG
שינויים פרונטו-טמפורליים ב- MRI
לימפוציטוזיס ב- CSF
keySource: IMA 2024-Sep Basic official answer key after appeals, Q146
explanation:
Viral encephalitis often causes altered mental status, CSF lymphocytic pleocytosis and normal CSF glucose. **EEG slowing, including high-amplitude slow activity, can occur in encephalitis.** Focal temporal periodic discharges are particularly suggestive of HSV in the right setting, but no listed EEG characteristic makes viral encephalitis incompatible.

**A. Normal CSF glucose.** Glucose is commonly preserved in viral encephalitis, although exceptions occur.
**B. High-amplitude slow EEG waves.** This nonspecific pattern may accompany diffuse cerebral dysfunction, including encephalitis. Amplitude alone neither confirms nor excludes infection.
**C. Frontotemporal MRI abnormalities.** These are compatible with HSV encephalitis, though other viral etiologies may have different distributions.
**D. CSF lymphocytosis.** A lymphocyte-predominant response is common. Early disease or immunosuppression may alter the CSF picture.

Reference · Harrison 22e, pp. 1112–1113. IDSA Management of Encephalitis guideline. Na et al., Encephalitis 2024, pp. 31–34, Figure 2.
Key note: In a PCR-confirmed herpes simplex encephalitis case, the EEG showed high-voltage frontotemporal sharp and theta waves followed by rhythmic delta slowing. The high-amplitude, slow-wave option cannot by itself exclude viral encephalitis.

q:
כל הרפלקסים הבאים קשורים לפגיעה בגזע המוח בחולה ב- Coma פרט לאחד.
איזה רפלקס לא קשור לפגיעה בגזע המוח?
o: PUPILARY LIGHT REACTION
OCULOVESTIBULAR REFLEX
CORNEAL REFLEX
DEEP TENDON REFLEX
keySource: IMA 2024-Sep Basic official answer key after appeals, Q147
explanation:
Bedside coma assessment tests brainstem pathways through pupil, eye-movement and corneal responses. **Deep tendon reflexes are the exception** because their immediate reflex arcs are spinal.

**A. Pupillary light reflex.** Afferent optic input and midbrain parasympathetic pathways drive the light response.
**B. Oculovestibular reflex.** Vestibular stimulation tests pontine and midbrain eye-movement connections.
**C. Corneal reflex.** Trigeminal afferent input and facial efferent output test a pontine reflex arc.
**D. Deep tendon reflex.** It assesses segmental spinal circuitry and descending influences, not a primary brainstem reflex.

Reference · Harrison 22e, p. 190.

q: איזה מהפרמטרים הבאים לא נכלל באומדן SOFA (Sepsis-related Organ Failure Assessment):
o: Platelets
Bilirubin
Creatinine
Respiratory rate
chapterTitle: Harrison 22e ch. 315 – Sepsis and Septic Shock
keySource: IMA 2024-Sep Basic official answer key after appeals, Q148
explanation:
Classic SOFA scores respiratory, coagulation, hepatic, cardiovascular, neurologic and renal dysfunction. **Respiratory rate is not the respiratory variable in full SOFA**. Oxygenation is assessed using the arterial oxygen to inspired oxygen ratio.

**A. Platelets.** Platelet count supplies the coagulation component.
**B. Bilirubin.** Bilirubin supplies the liver component.
**C. Creatinine.** Creatinine or urine output supplies the renal component.
**D. Respiratory rate.** Respiratory rate is used in qSOFA, which is a different bedside screen.

Reference · Harrison 22e, pp. 2316–2317.

o: US בטן
PEP
ANA
אקו
chapterTitle: Harrison 22e ch. 22 – Fever of Unknown Origin
keySource: IMA 2024-Sep Basic official answer key after appeals, Q149
explanation:
Fever of unknown origin requires a standardized initial evaluation before clue-directed testing. **Echocardiography is the exception to the universal initial list** here and is particularly valuable when endocarditis is suspected.

**A. Abdominal ultrasound.** This screens for occult abdominal causes in the obligatory initial work-up.
**B. Protein electrophoresis.** It can reveal an abnormal protein pattern suggesting a plasma cell or inflammatory disorder and belongs to the initial panel.
**C. ANA.** An antinuclear antibody test is part of the initial search for inflammatory or autoimmune clues.
**D. Echocardiography.** Order it when history, cultures, examination or other findings raise suspicion of a cardiac focus.

Reference · Harrison 22e, pp. 149, 152.
Key note: All four were accepted as exceptions. Harrison includes abdominal ultrasound, protein electrophoresis and ANA among the obligatory tests and reserves echocardiography for appropriate clinical clues.

q: כל התרופות הבאות גורמות לנויטרופניה פרט ל-
o: Clozapine
Carbamazepine
Lithium
Chloramphenicol
chapterTitle: Harrison 22e ch. 67 – Disorders of Granulocytes and Monocytes
keySource: IMA 2024-Sep Basic official answer key after appeals, Q150
explanation:
Neutropenia can be an important drug toxicity, sometimes progressing to agranulocytosis. **Lithium is the exception** among these medicines because it more often raises neutrophils.

**A. Clozapine.** Clozapine can cause severe neutropenia and requires appropriate blood-count monitoring.
**B. Carbamazepine.** Carbamazepine can suppress white-cell production and occasionally cause serious cytopenias.
**C. Lithium.** Lithium tends to stimulate neutrophil production, causing neutrophilia rather than the characteristic drug-induced neutropenia asked about.
**D. Chloramphenicol.** Chloramphenicol can suppress bone marrow and cause cytopenias.

Reference · Harrison 22e, pp. 457–458.

q: מה מאפיין SPINAL CORD COMPRESSION?
o: המקום השכיח ביותר הוא בעמוד השדרה התורקלי
הסיבה השכיחה היא גרורה ממקור של המעי הגס
בדרך כלל הביטוי הראשון הוא חולשת שרירים דיסטלית למקום הנזק
הכאב מוחמר בישיבה
keySource: IMA 2024-May Basic official answer key after appeals, Q101
explanation:
Malignant spinal cord compression most often involves the **thoracic spine**. **Weakness below the level of compression** is an important neurologic sign, but localized back pain commonly precedes it.

**A. Thoracic predominance.** The thoracic spine accounts for most malignant cord compressions.
**B. Colorectal cancer predominates.** Lung, breast and prostate cancers are common causes. Colorectal cancer is not the leading primary.
**C. Weakness is usually first.** Weakness below the lesion is clinically important. Calling it the usual first symptom misses the earlier pain phase.
**D. Pain worse sitting.** Supine pain and pain with coughing, sneezing or movement are more characteristic clues.

Reference · Harrison 22e, p. 588.
Key note: Harrison identifies localized back pain and tenderness as the most common initial symptom. The exam also credits distal weakness as the usual first manifestation.

q: מה המשפט המתאר נכונה בירור של פוליציטמיה?
o: אריתרופואטין נמוך מכוון להרעלת CO.
אריתרופואטין גבוה מכוון ל- POLYCYTHEMIA VERA
אריתרופואטין גבוה מחייב בירור לגידול מפריש אריתרופואטין
ברוב האנשים עם אריתרופואטין נמוך תימצא מוטציה ב- JAK2
keySource: IMA 2024-May Basic official answer key after appeals, Q102
explanation:
Erythropoietin helps distinguish autonomous erythrocytosis from a response to hypoxia or another secondary stimulus. **Low EPO should prompt evaluation for polycythemia vera, including JAK2 testing.** Most patients with established PV carry JAK2 mutations, but that statistic does not tell us what proportion of all low-EPO patients have one.

**A. Low EPO suggests carbon monoxide.** Carbon monoxide causes tissue hypoxia and favors secondary erythrocytosis rather than autonomous erythroid production.
**B. High EPO suggests PV.** PV often suppresses EPO through feedback. Elevated EPO instead prompts assessment for secondary causes.
**C. High EPO requires a tumor workup.** First assess oxygenation, exposure, medications and other causes. Persistent unexplained elevation or suggestive findings warrant evaluation for renal or other EPO-producing tumors.
**D. Most people with low EPO have JAK2.** In a patient with confirmed erythrocytosis, a low EPO strongly supports PV and prompts JAK2 testing. The predictive value depends on clinical selection. A percentage measured in patients with known PV cannot be transferred directly to every person with low EPO.

Reference · Harrison 22e, pp. 451–452. Mossuz et al., Diagnostic Value of Serum Erythropoietin Level in Patients With Absolute Erythrocytosis, Haematologica 2004, PMID 15477203.

q:
בן 78, ברקע יתר לחץ דם, דיכאון וסוכרת עבר בירור להפרעות שינה ואובחן כסובל מ- Obstructive Sleep Apnea ברמה חמורה. ניסה טיפול ב- CPAP שהופסק אחרי שבוע עקב אי סבילות.
מה ניתן להציע לו?
o: התייעצות מומחה להתאמת ה- CPAP
טיפול תרופתי ב- ZOPICLONE (NOCTURNO)
טיפול תרופתי ב- CLONAZEPAM (CLONEX)
יעוץ אף אוזן גרון בשאלה של ניתוח
keySource: IMA 2024-May Basic official answer key after appeals, Q103
explanation:
Severe obstructive sleep apnea requires effective treatment even when a first CPAP trial is uncomfortable. **Specialist adjustment of CPAP and, for selected persistent intolerance, surgical evaluation** are both reasonable routes.

**A. Specialist CPAP support.** Troubleshoot mask, pressure, leaks and nasal symptoms after a short unsuccessful trial.
**B. Zopiclone.** A hypnotic treats sleep symptoms but does not splint open an obstructed airway.
**C. Clonazepam.** Sedation does not correct obstruction and can add respiratory and fall risk.
**D. ENT surgical assessment.** Selected patients who cannot tolerate effective positive-pressure treatment may have an anatomic target. Evaluation does not guarantee that surgery will help.

Reference · Harrison 22e, p. 2281.

q: באיזה מהבאים מתואר ממצא בבדיקה הגופנית המתאים לבעיה המסתמית המפורטת?
o: PULSUS PARADOXUS ב- AORTIC STENOSIS
לחץ דם ביד גבוה מלחץ הדם ברגל ב- AORTIC INSUFFICIENCY
צרידות בקול ב- MITRAL STENOSIS
PULSUS PARVUS et TARDUS ב- MITRAL INSUFFICIENCY
keySource: IMA 2024-May Basic official answer key after appeals, Q104
explanation:
Mitral stenosis elevates left atrial pressure and can enlarge the atrium. Compression of the left recurrent laryngeal nerve can then produce hoarseness, called Ortner syndrome.
**Hoarseness is the correctly paired finding in mitral stenosis.**

**A. Pulsus paradoxus in aortic stenosis.** Pulsus paradoxus describes an exaggerated inspiratory fall in systolic blood pressure. The characteristic carotid pulse of aortic stenosis is small and delayed.
**B. Arm pressure above leg pressure in aortic regurgitation.** Hill sign runs in the opposite direction. Leg systolic pressure exceeds arm systolic pressure.
**C. Hoarseness in mitral stenosis.** An enlarged left atrium can impair the left recurrent laryngeal nerve. New atrial fibrillation, embolism or dyspnea can also bring the patient to attention.
**D. Pulsus parvus et tardus in mitral regurgitation.** This weak, late-rising carotid pulse reflects obstruction to aortic outflow. Mitral regurgitation produces systolic backward flow into the atrium.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 1150, 1154, 1156, including Table 75-4.

q: לאיזה מהגידולים הבאים יש סיכוי לריפוי מלא עם טיפול כימותרפי בלבד?
o: BLADDER CARCINOMA
SMALL CELL LUNG CARCINOMA
GASTRIC CARCINOMA
PROSTATE CARCINOMA
chapterTitle: Harrison 22e ch. 78 – Principles of Cancer Treatment
keySource: IMA 2024-May Basic official answer key after appeals, Q105
explanation:
Some tumors are highly sensitive to cytotoxic chemotherapy. **Small-cell lung carcinoma** is the listed cancer in which cure with systemic chemotherapy alone is possible in a minority. Possible cure should not be read as a claim that radiation has no role.

**A. Bladder carcinoma.** Systemic chemotherapy can produce responses in urothelial cancer, but curative treatment of localized disease usually includes local therapy.
**B. Small-cell lung carcinoma.** SCLC can respond dramatically; limited-stage disease is usually treated with combined chemotherapy and thoracic radiation when feasible.
**C. Gastric carcinoma.** Localized gastric cancer generally requires resection as part of curative management.
**D. Prostate carcinoma.** Chemotherapy for advanced prostate cancer can prolong survival but is not typically curative by itself.

Reference · Harrison 22e, pp. 556, 558.
